  • Calendars.Read - Read user calendars and events
  • Calendars.Read.Shared - Read calendars user can access, including shared

User directory

  • User.ReadBasic.All - Read basic profiles of all users (for meeting availability)

Chat permissions

  • Chat.Read - Read user chat messages
  • Chat.ReadBasic - Read user chat metadata (alternative for limited functionality)
  • ChatMember.Read - Read the members of chats
  • ChatMessage.Read - Read user chat messages (more specific than Chat.Read)

Channel permissions

  • Team.ReadBasic.All - Read the names and descriptions of teams
  • Channel.ReadBasic.All - Read the names and descriptions of channels
  • ChannelMessage.Read.All - Read channel messages

Meeting permissions

  • OnlineMeetings.Read - Read online meetings
  • OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All - Read meeting transcripts
  • OnlineMeetingAiInsight.Read - Read all AI Insights for online meetings
  • OnlineMeetingArtifact.Read.All - Read user’s online meeting artifacts
  • OnlineMeetingRecording.Read.All - Read all recordings of online meetings

Files permissions

  • Files.Read - Read user files
  • Files.Read.All - Read all files user can access

Sites permissions

  • Sites.Read.All - Read items in all site collections

Write permissions

Requested as part of the updated consent set; used only when write tools are enabled:

  • Mail.Send - Send and forward email
  • Mail.ReadWrite - Create, update, and delete drafts; move and label messages
  • Calendars.ReadWrite - Create, update, delete, and respond to calendar events
  • Files.ReadWrite.All - Create, update, and delete files and folders in OneDrive and SharePoint
  • MailboxSettings.ReadWrite - Manage categories, inbox rules, and automatic replies
  • ChatMessage.Send - Send a Teams chat message on the user’s behalf
  • ChannelMessage.Send - Post or reply in a Teams channel
  • Chat.Create - Start a new Teams chat on the user’s behalf
  • People.Read: Find people in the organization to start a chat with
Current limitations
  • Teams write access is limited to messaging: Claude can send a chat message, post or reply in a channel, or start a new chat, but can’t modify Teams settings, memberships, or permissions. All write tools require an admin to enable them.
  • User-level access only: Access with service principal authentication is not supported.
  • Online Archive mailboxes aren’t searched: email search covers each user’s primary mailbox, including its Archive folder, and any shared mailboxes they can access. It doesn’t cover the separate Online Archive mailbox (also called the In-Place Archive), so messages that a retention policy has moved there won’t appear in results.
Frequently asked questions

Can we test with a small pilot group before enterprise-wide rollout?

Yes. The recommended approach is to use app assignment to restrict who can use the connector:

  • Enable the connector (Team and Enterprise Owners enable it in organization settings; individual plan users can connect directly).
  • Microsoft Entra Admin completes pre-consent setup
  • Use Microsoft Entra Enterprise App assignment to restrict access to specific users or groups (e.g., assign only “IT Security Test Group” to the app).
  • Expand groups progressively for gradual deployment

How do we ensure no data leakage occurs between our organization and others in the multi-tenant environment?

Multi-tenant isolation ensures complete separation:

  • Server uses the common tenant configuration to accept tokens from any Microsoft Entra ID tenant
  • Each user’s token contains their organization’s tenant ID (tid claim) which is validated
  • Graph API tokens obtained through OBO are automatically scoped to the user and their tenant
  • Cross-tenant token access is prevented cryptographically by the design of Microsoft Graph’s OAuth 2.0 implementation.

What happens if someone tries to connect with a personal Microsoft account?

It depends on which option they choose:

  • Work or school option: Signing in with a personal account gives an authentication error.
  • Personal account option: On Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, people can connect a personal account here. This option isn’t shown on Team and Enterprise plans.

Learn more about personal Microsoft accounts.

Do you have audit logging for compliance?

Yes. All Graph API calls made by the connector are logged in your organization’s Microsoft 365 audit log, which you can access through the M365 Compliance Center. These logs show the timestamp, user, operation performed, and resource accessed, with retention periods matching your Microsoft 365 audit policy. Additionally, Anthropic logs authentication and tool execution events.

Can we revoke access if we discover unauthorized usage?

There are multiple revocation methods:

  • Individual: Users disconnect via Customize > Connectors
  • Admin-level: On Team and Enterprise plans, Owners disable the connector in Claude organization settings (all team members affected).
  • Permission-level: Revoke specific permissions in Microsoft Entra Admin Center
  • Tenant-level: Revoke all permissions in Microsoft Entra Admin Center

Personal Microsoft accounts

On Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, people can connect a personal Microsoft account, such as an Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live, or MSN account. This option isn’t shown on Team and Enterprise plans. Learn more in Connect to Microsoft 365.

  • Separate applications: Personal accounts use their own Microsoft applications, which accept only personal accounts. Your tenant’s applications and consent aren’t involved.
  • Consent: Each person consents for their own account. There’s no admin step, and Microsoft Entra controls such as Conditional Access and app assignment don’t apply.
  • Tools: Personal accounts get the tools in Available capabilities, plus search_people, except the Teams tools, chat_message_search, find_meeting_availability, outlook_create_filter, outlook_delete_filter, and outlook_set_vacation. read_resource can’t read Teams content. The sharepoint_* tools work on the person’s own OneDrive, including shared items they’ve added to it, and don’t use Sites.Read.All.
  • Write tools: There’s no admin setting, so write tools are available once connected. Attribution, rate limits, and the attachment restriction still apply. The “Always allow” limits in Available capabilities don’t apply to personal accounts.
  • Permissions: Personal accounts request these Microsoft Graph permissions: User.Read, offline_access, Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, MailboxSettings.Read, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read, Calendars.ReadWrite, Files.Read.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, and People.Read. Sign-in also requests openid and email, so Claude receives the account’s email address.
  • Terms: On Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, this connection falls under Anthropic’s Consumer Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
  • Access removal: People disconnect in Customize > Connectors and can remove the permission in their Microsoft account.
  • Data handling: The connector retrieves data on demand and doesn’t cache file content. Your email and files stay in your Microsoft account, but content Claude retrieves becomes part of your chat. Credentials are encrypted and managed by Anthropic’s backend infrastructure, and the connector doesn’t see or store passwords. Tool call results in stored chats are retained.

Certifications

Anthropic has the following certifications:

  • SOC 2 Type II (annual audit)
  • ISO 27001 certified
  • DPA available on Team and Enterprise plans

Set up the Microsoft 365 connector

This article walks admins through enabling the Microsoft 365 connector for their organization in Claude—including granting Microsoft Entra consent, restricting access, and managing permissions. Once setup is complete, people in your tenant can connect Microsoft 365 to their own Claude accounts to search across SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, and Teams from Claude. You can also enable write tools, which let Claude send email, manage calendar events, create and update files, and send Teams messages on a member’s behalf.

The Microsoft 365 connector is available on all Claude plans: Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise.

For end-user instructions on connecting and using Microsoft 365 once setup is complete, see Connect to Microsoft 365.

Important: This article covers work and school accounts, which require a Microsoft Entra tenant. Personal Microsoft accounts need no admin setup and aren’t shown on Team and Enterprise plans. Learn more in Connect to Microsoft 365.

Setup overview

Two things need to happen before anyone in your organization can connect Microsoft 365, plus an optional third step if you want to enable write tools:

  • On Team and Enterprise plans: A Claude organization owner enables the Microsoft 365 connector for the organization.
  • In every tenant: A Microsoft Entra Global Administrator grants a one-time consent that authorizes the integration for your tenant.
  • To enable write tools: A Microsoft Entra administrator consents to the updated permission set, and you enable write tools for your organization. See Enable write tools below.

After completing these steps, members can connect Microsoft 365 to their own Claude accounts following the steps in Connect to Microsoft 365.

Enable the connector for your organization

This step applies to Team and Enterprise plans only. On Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, skip to the next section.

  • Sign in to Claude.
  • Navigate to Organization settings > Connectors.
  • Click “+ Add” at the top of the page, then “All available.”
  • Find Microsoft 365 and click “Add to your team.”

Grant Microsoft Entra admin consent

A Microsoft Entra Global Administrator in your tenant needs to authorize the integration before anyone can connect. There are two ways to do this.

Option 1: Consent through Claude

If your Microsoft Entra Global Administrator has a Claude account, they can grant consent during the standard connection flow:

  • Navigate to Customize > Connectors.
  • Find Microsoft 365 and click “Connect.”
  • Choose “Work or school account,” if you’re asked.
  • Authenticate with Microsoft 365 credentials.
  • Review and accept the requested permissions, checking the box to grant access on behalf of the whole organization.

After this, other people in the same Entra tenant can connect by following the standard end-user steps. They won’t see the consent prompt—they’ll just authenticate and start using the integration.

Option 2: Manual setup in Microsoft Entra ID

Use this path if your Microsoft Entra Global Administrator doesn’t have a Claude account, or if you need to troubleshoot the app install and permissions setup. You can add the connector apps and grant admin consent directly in Microsoft Entra ID.

This process adds two service principals to your tenant. Each principal establishes a service-level identity for one of the two M365 MCP for Claude app registrations, allowing them to access and interact with your organization’s data and resources via the Microsoft Graph API.

  1. Add the service principals

Using Microsoft Graph Explorer, add both required service principals:

M365 MCP Client for Claude:

POST [graph.microsoft.com](https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals)
{"appId":"08ad6f98-a4f8-4635-bb8d-f1a3044760f0"}

M365 MCP Server for Claude:

POST [graph.microsoft.com](https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals)
{"appId":"07c030f6-5743-41b7-ba00-0a6e85f37c17"}
  1. Grant admin consent

Construct and visit the following URLs in your browser, replacing {your-tenant-id} with your organization’s tenant ID.

M365 MCP Client for Claude:

[login.microsoftonline.com](https://login.microsoftonline.com/{your-tenant-id}/adminconsent?client_id=08ad6f98-a4f8-4635-bb8d-f1a3044760f0)

M365 MCP Server for Claude:

[login.microsoftonline.com](https://login.microsoftonline.com/{your-tenant-id}/adminconsent?client_id=07c030f6-5743-41b7-ba00-0a6e85f37c17)

When you visit each URL, you’ll be prompted to consent to the delegated permissions required by the integration on behalf of your organization.

  1. Finish setup
  • Team and Enterprise plans: A Claude organization Owner needs to enable the connector in Organization settings > Connectors. Then members can connect individually.
  • Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans: Members can connect by navigating to Customize > Connectors, finding Microsoft 365, and clicking “Connect.” They choose “Work or school account,” if they’re asked.
Restrict who can use the connector

To limit which people in your tenant can authenticate to Microsoft 365 through Claude:

  • Go to the Microsoft Entra admin center at entra.microsoft.com.
  • Navigate to the M365 MCP Server for Claude enterprise application.
  • Go to Properties and set Assignment required? to “Yes.”
  • Under Users and groups, add the specific users or groups who should have access.
  • Repeat the same steps for the M365 MCP Client for Claude enterprise application.

Both components need to be restricted to the same set of authorized people.

Restrict which permissions the connector can use

To limit which types of resources the integration can access, selectively revoke permissions from the default set of authorized scopes. This requires Microsoft Entra admin access.

  • As a Microsoft Entra admin, go to entra.microsoft.com.
  • Select “Enterprise Applications.”
  • Next to the search box, remove the application type filter.
  • Search for and click “M365 MCP Server for Claude.”
  • Go to Permissions.
  • Under the Admin consent tab and in the Microsoft Graph list of permissions, select the permission you would like to revoke and click the “…” button.
  • Select “Revoke permission” and confirm with “Yes, revoke.”

Once revoked, attempts to access a resource with that permission will return a “Failed to call tool” error.

Members can also individually turn off specific tools in their own Microsoft 365 settings to prevent Claude from trying to access a tool for which the permission has been revoked.

To restore a revoked permission, follow the steps to grant admin consent described in Option 2: Manual setup in Microsoft Entra ID. This will revert the permissions to the default state.

Enable write tools

Write tools let Claude send email, manage drafts and calendar events, update mailbox settings, and create and update files in OneDrive and SharePoint, and send messages in Microsoft Teams. Read and search tools work the same whether or not write tools are enabled.

  1. Re-consent to the updated permissions

The connector’s permission set now includes additional Microsoft Graph scopes to support write tools. If your tenant consented before write tools or the Teams write tools launched, a Microsoft Entra Global Administrator needs to review and approve the updated permission set before write tools activate. Review and approve the updated permissions for the connector in your tenant’s Enterprise Applications consent flow.

  1. Enable write tools for your organization

Go to Organization settings > Connectors, find “Microsoft 365,” and choose a setting for each write tool: Always allow, Needs approval, or Blocked. Your changes apply as soon as you save. Enterprise plans can enable write tools for a subset of users through custom roles.

For Microsoft Teams specifically, set each Teams write tool individually: the send, post, and reply tools can be set to Needs approval or Blocked (members confirm each send), and starting a new chat can also be set to Always allow. If your organization added the Microsoft 365 connector for the first time after November 9, 2026, the send, post, and reply tools can also be set to Always allow, and members can then choose Always allow for them. Removing the connector and adding it again usually keeps your organization’s original install date.

If you see a notice about these tools, you can set them to Always allow now in Review write tools, in Review tool restrictions, or on the Tools tab. The limit ends right away for each tool you set to Always allow, and members can then choose Always allow for it. Some members may have chosen Always allow for that tool in the past. That earlier choice can take effect right away, so Claude can stop asking them. Outside “Automatically approve” mode, Claude asks everyone else by default until they choose it.

If you have more than one Microsoft 365 connector, save the tool on each one. An Always allow saved before November 9, 2026 doesn’t end the limit until you save it again. For the rest of these tools, members must still approve each use until the limit is removed on or after December 9, 2026. Any of these tools you haven’t set by then will change to Needs approval, unless the whole connector is set to Blocked.

Changes you save apply right away. A tool set to Always allow turns on right away if it was blocked by default. With Always allow, Claude may use a tool without asking anyone first, including in “Automatically approve” mode and in some scheduled tasks, such as a cloud scheduled task set to “Automatically approve” or a Claude Code routine. Scheduled tasks can lose access to tools on Needs approval. In Cowork, members can choose Always allow for write tools only when the organization setting Allow “Always allow” for connector tools is on.

Setting a connector’s default restriction to No restriction doesn’t turn on a tool that is blocked by default.

Organizations that have enabled HIPAA aren’t part of these changes to default blocks and limits: they don’t get a notice, and neither setting Always allow nor adding the connector for the first time ends this limit.

If your Team or Enterprise organization added the connector before November 9, 2026, two limits apply until at least December 9, 2026:

  • If your organization was using the connector before write tools or the Teams write tools launched, some write tools are blocked by default until at least December 9, 2026. To turn them on sooner, go to Organization settings > Connectors, find “Microsoft 365,” and choose a setting for each tool. On or after December 9, 2026, any tool that is still blocked by default will be set to Needs approval, unless the whole connector is set to Blocked. If one of these tools is among the 11 Outlook, Calendar, and Teams tools with a limit that Anthropic will remove on or after that date, you can set it to Always allow now. It turns on right away. Once it’s saved on each of your Microsoft 365 connectors, the limit ends for that tool, and members can choose Always allow for it. Claude may then use it without asking anyone first, including in “Automatically approve” mode and in some scheduled tasks, such as a cloud scheduled task set to “Automatically approve” or a Claude Code routine. Scheduled tasks can lose access to tools on Needs approval. Organizations that have enabled HIPAA aren’t part of these changes to default blocks and limits. Enterprise plans can enable write tools for a subset of users through custom roles.
  • Users can’t choose Always allow for 11 tools, so in chat and Cowork, they confirm each use. These are the tools that send email or Teams messages, create, change, delete, or respond to calendar events, or set automatic replies. Starting a new Teams chat is not one of them and can be set to Always allow.

Both limits end on or after December 9, 2026. See Coming on or after December 9, 2026: changes to write tools below.

  1. Verify

Once enabled, ask Claude to perform a low-risk write action, such as “Draft an email to myself, but don’t send it,” to confirm write tools are active.

Note: Emails Claude sends include an attribution header identifying them as agent-initiated. File writes, calendar writes, and Teams messages aren’t currently tagged. When Claude creates or updates a calendar event, Microsoft 365 automatically sends attendees an invitation or update notice. Attachments aren’t supported in write tools, so sending, forwarding, and drafting all reject messages with attachments. Write tools are also subject to per-user limits on writes, sends, and recipients.

Coming on or after December 9, 2026: changes to write tools

This applies to Team and Enterprise organizations that added the Microsoft 365 connector before November 9, 2026.

On or after December 9, 2026, Anthropic will remove a limit on 11 tools. Until then, in chat and Cowork, Claude asks users before every use of these tools.

The 11 tools:

  • Outlook: send an email, forward an email, send a draft, set automatic replies
  • Calendar: create, change, delete, or respond to an event
  • Teams: send a chat message, post in a channel, reply in a channel

What you can do now:

  • Choose a setting for any write tool. Your changes apply as soon as you save.
  • If you see a notice about these tools, you can set them to Always allow now. Users must still approve each use until the limit is removed.
  • A blocked tool turns on right away when you set it to Always allow or Needs approval.
  • A cloud scheduled task set to Automatically approve, or a Claude Code routine, can use a tool set to Always allow without asking anyone. Scheduled tasks can lose access to tools on Needs approval.

When the limit is removed:

  • Any of the 11 tools you have not set individually will be set to Needs approval, even if the connector’s default restriction is No restriction.
  • Settings you have saved are kept. A tool you set to Blocked stays Blocked.
  • Users can choose Always allow for one of these tools only if you set that tool to Always allow. In Cowork, Allow “Always allow” for connector tools must also be on. It is off by default.
  • Write tools that are still blocked by default, and that you have not changed, will be turned on and set to Needs approval. To keep a tool off, set it to Blocked.
  • If you have set the whole connector to Blocked, its tools stay blocked.

Removing the connector and adding it again doesn’t remove the limit. Organizations that add the connector for the first time after November 9, 2026 don’t have it.

Permissions reference

The Microsoft 365 connector uses delegated permissions, meaning Claude acts on behalf of each individual user and can only access data that user already has permission to view in Microsoft 365. Permissions are read-only by default. Claude can only send, create, or update content if you enable write tools.

During authentication, the integration requests the following permissions:

Basic access

  • User.Read: Sign in and read user profile
  • openid: Sign in with organizational account
  • offline_access: Maintain access to data
  • email: View email address
  • profile: View basic profile information

Email (Outlook)

  • Mail.Read: Read email messages
  • Mail.ReadBasic: Read email metadata (sender, subject, date)
  • Mail.Read.Shared: Read emails in mailboxes the user has access to
    • Note: Shared mailbox access is included through the Mail.Read.Shared permission. Users can search shared mailboxes they have delegate access to in Microsoft 365, including full access and folder-level delegation. No setup is needed beyond standard admin consent and the delegate permissions already configured in Microsoft 365.
  • MailboxFolder.Read: Read mailbox folder structure
  • MailboxItem.Read: Read items in mailbox
  • MailboxSettings.Read: Read mailbox settings, like the user’s timezone

Note: Email search covers each user’s primary mailbox, including its Archive folder, and any shared mailboxes they can access. It doesn’t cover the separate Online Archive mailbox (also called the In-Place Archive), so messages that a retention policy has moved there won’t appear in results.

Calendar

  • Calendars.Read: Read calendar events
  • Calendars.Read.Shared: Read calendars shared with the user

Teams chat

  • Chat.Read: Read Teams chat messages
  • Chat.ReadBasic: Read Teams chat metadata
  • ChatMember.Read: Read information about chat participants
  • ChatMessage.Read: Read Teams chat messages

Teams channels

  • Team.ReadBasic.All: Read the names and descriptions of teams
  • Channel.ReadBasic.All: Read channel names and descriptions
  • ChannelMessage.Read.All: Read channel messages

Meetings

  • OnlineMeetings.Read: Read online meetings
  • OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All: Read meeting transcripts
  • OnlineMeetingAiInsight.Read: Read AI-generated meeting insights
  • OnlineMeetingArtifact.Read.All: Read meeting recordings and artifacts
  • OnlineMeetingRecording.Read.All: Read meeting recordings

Note: By default, Microsoft doesn’t let apps access Teams meeting transcripts, whatever permissions they’ve been granted. To let Claude read transcripts, have a Teams admin go to Meetings > Meeting settings in the Teams admin center and turn on Microsoft Graph access under Transcript API access. To include speaker attribution, select “Configure” and turn on Include speaker attribution, which is also off by default. Learn more in Microsoft’s guide to transcript API access.

Files (OneDrive and SharePoint)

  • Files.Read: Read user files
  • Files.Read.All: Read all files the user can access
  • Sites.Read.All: Read items in SharePoint sites

Write permissions

The following permissions support write tools and are included in the updated consent set:

  • Mail.Send: Send and forward email
  • Mail.ReadWrite: Create, update, and delete drafts; move and label messages
  • Calendars.ReadWrite: Create, update, delete, and respond to calendar events
  • Files.ReadWrite.All: Create, update, and delete files and folders in OneDrive and SharePoint. Deleted items go to the recycle bin.
  • MailboxSettings.ReadWrite: Manage categories, inbox rules, and automatic replies
  • ChatMessage.Send: Send a Teams chat message on the user’s behalf
  • ChannelMessage.Send: Post or reply in a Teams channel
  • Chat.Create: Start a new chat on the user’s behalf
  • People.Read: Find people in the organization to start a chat with

User directory

  • User.ReadBasic.All: Read basic profile information for all users in the organization (used for finding meeting availability)

The Microsoft 365 connector searches SharePoint across the entire tenant using the permissions of the user. Site-specific search restriction isn’t supported.

Privacy and security

  • Permission inheritance: Claude mirrors each user’s existing Microsoft 365 permissions. Members can’t access anything through Claude that they couldn’t already see directly in Microsoft 365.
  • On your request. Claude accesses Microsoft 365 when you ask, or when a scheduled task you set up needs it.
  • Revocable access: Members can disconnect their own integration through Customize > Connectors. Team and Enterprise plan Owners can also remove the connector for the entire organization in Organization settings > Connectors.

For more detail, see the Microsoft 365 connector security guide.

Troubleshooting

A member can’t authenticate
  • Confirm their account is tied to a Microsoft Entra tenant, not a personal Microsoft account.
  • Confirm their Microsoft 365 license is active.
  • Confirm admin consent has been granted using Option 1 or Option 2 above.
  • Check whether a Conditional Access policy in your tenant is blocking the connection. See below: Conditional Access is blocking the connection.
Members are seeing “Failed to call tool” errors

A permission may have been selectively revoked in Microsoft Entra. Members can turn off the corresponding tool in their Microsoft 365 settings to suppress the error, or you can restore the permission by repeating the admin consent steps in Option 2: Manual setup in Microsoft Entra ID.

A Teams tool returns a 403 “Missing scope” error

The connector’s permission set now includes Team.ReadBasic.All, which Claude needs to list the teams a user belongs to. If your tenant consented before this permission was added, Teams tools that rely on it return a 403 “Missing scope” error. To fix it, have a Microsoft Entra Global Administrator repeat the admin consent steps in Option 1: Consent through Claude or Option 2: Manual setup in Microsoft Entra ID.

Note: Repeating admin consent grants the connector’s full current permission set, including the write permissions. If you revoked any write permissions on purpose, revoke them again afterward.

Write tools aren’t appearing for members
  • Confirm a Microsoft Entra administrator has consented to the updated permission set that includes write scopes.
  • Confirm write tools are enabled in the Microsoft 365 connector configuration, or that the member is covered by a role-based access policy that grants them.
  • Have the member disconnect and reconnect Microsoft 365 in Customize > Connectors.
Claude doesn’t find files that SharePoint search finds

This only applies when SharePoint’s own search finds a file and Claude doesn’t. When Claude searches SharePoint and OneDrive files, it adds isDocument=true to every query, so it only finds files that your tenant’s search index marks as documents. If the index doesn’t mark some files, Claude won’t find them, and no error is shown.

To check whether this is the cause:

  • Sign in to Graph Explorer as a user who can open a missing file. Consent to Files.Read.All, if you’re asked.

  • Run this search, replacing budget with a word from the missing file. Choose a word that few other files contain:

    POST graph.microsoft.com {“requests”:[{“entityTypes”:[“driveItem”],“query”:{“queryString”:” (budget)“},”size”:100,“sortProperties”: [{“name”:“LastModifiedTime”,“isDescending”:true}]}]}

  • Run it again with the document filter added, using the same word:

    POST graph.microsoft.com {“requests”:[{“entityTypes”:[“driveItem”],“query”:{“queryString”:“(budget) AND isDocument=true”},“size”:100,“sortProperties”: [{“name”:“LastModifiedTime”,“isDescending”:true}]}]}

  • Compare the results:

    • If a Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or PDF file you expected appears only in the first search, your search index isn’t marking it as a document. Open a case with Microsoft Support and share both searches.
    • If the file doesn’t appear in either search, this isn’t the cause.
Conditional Access is blocking the connection

A Conditional Access block shows up in one of three ways:

  • A user sees “Authorization with the MCP server failed” and a reference code starting with ofid_ when they try to connect. Our Support team can look up that code.
  • A member who is already connected gets an error when Claude uses a Microsoft 365 tool. The error includes an AADSTS code, a note that the request was blocked by a Conditional Access policy, and the Trace ID and Correlation ID you can search for in Entra.
  • Members are asked to reconnect Microsoft 365 on a regular cycle, much more often than the normal 90-day expiry. This usually means a sign-in frequency policy.

Connecting Microsoft 365 involves more than the sign-in the member sees. After the member signs in to Microsoft in their browser, Claude’s servers exchange that sign-in for access tokens, and later exchange those tokens for Microsoft 365 access on the member’s behalf. In our testing, Entra evaluates your Conditional Access policies against these server-side requests as coming from Anthropic’s outbound IP addresses. They identify the member and carry the device recorded when the member connected, not the member’s current device or network. So a policy can pass the member’s own sign-in and still block the connection a moment later, or block it days later. Learn more about Anthropic’s outbound IP addresses

Find the policy that’s blocking the connection

  • In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Sign-in logs and open the User sign-ins (non-interactive) tab. The member’s own sign-in appears on the interactive tab and usually shows as successful, so the block is rarely there.
  • Filter by the affected member. The blocked requests can appear under either M365 MCP Server for Claude or M365 MCP Client for Claude, so filtering by member is more reliable than filtering by application. Don’t filter by resource, which hides some of the rows.
  • Open the failed entry and select the Conditional Access tab. It names the policy that blocked the request.

The error code tells you what kind of policy it is:

  • AADSTS70043: a sign-in frequency policy. See the next section.
  • AADSTS53003: a policy set to block access. The Conditional Access tab tells you which one. If it’s based on location, see the next section.
  • AADSTS50076: a policy required multi-factor authentication on a server-side request. Disconnecting and reconnecting Microsoft 365 clears it. If it keeps happening, see the Microsoft 365 connector security guide.
  • AADSTS53000: a policy requires a compliant device. The similar code AADSTS530003 means a policy requires a managed device. In both cases the member needs to reconnect from a device that meets the policy. Learn more in the Microsoft 365 connector security guide.

Exclude Anthropic’s IP ranges from sign-in frequency and location policies

Because the server-side requests come from Anthropic’s IP ranges, a policy that limits sign-ins to your own network, or that enforces a sign-in frequency, blocks them for every member. Excluding the two Claude applications from the policy isn’t enough on its own. We recommend excluding Anthropic’s IP ranges from the policy as well.

Note: Don’t use this exclusion for a device compliance policy. The server-side requests carry the device recorded when the member connected, so a device policy still applies to them, and excluding Anthropic’s IP ranges would turn the device check off for the connector. Members blocked by a device policy need to reconnect from a device that meets it. Learn more in the Microsoft 365 connector security guide.

If the policy that blocked the request is a sign-in frequency or location policy:

  • In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Conditional Access > Named locations and create an IP range location. Add every current IPv4 range, in full, from Anthropic’s Outbound IP addresses list. Leave Mark as trusted location unchecked so the exclusion doesn’t affect other policies that use trusted locations. If Anthropic adds a range to that list, add it to this location too.
  • Open the policy that blocked the request and go to Conditions > Locations > Exclude.
  • Add the named location you created. Keep any existing exclusions for the Claude applications in place.
  • Save the policy and wait a few minutes for the change to apply.
  • Have an affected member disconnect and reconnect Microsoft 365 in Customize > Connectors.

Note: Excluding the ranges lifts the policy for every request that comes from Anthropic’s addresses, which means all Microsoft 365 connector activity for all of your members. For a sign-in frequency policy, this also means the connector’s background requests are no longer subject to it, so a connection stays signed in until it expires after 90 days of inactivity. If you’d rather keep the periodic reconnects, leave the policy as it is. Members who are asked to reconnect can sign out of Microsoft in their browser, or use a private browsing window, before reconnecting. If you want to check the effect of a change before making it, clone the policy in report-only mode first.

Frequently asked questions

What happens if a member tries to connect before consent is granted?

They’ll see an error message indicating that an administrator must grant app permissions before they can use the integration. The connection will fail until a Microsoft Entra Global Administrator approves the necessary permissions.

Can the Microsoft 365 connector be used with enterprise search?

Yes. When enterprise search is enabled, it can query Microsoft 365 alongside other connected services for unified search across Slack, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and more.

What file types can the connector read?

Claude reads Word, Excel, PowerPoint (including older .doc, .xls, and .ppt files), PDF, and plain-text formats such as .txt, .md, and .csv from SharePoint and OneDrive. Other formats, including OneNote, can’t be read. For the full list, see Connect to Microsoft 365.

Can the integration modify Microsoft 365 data?

Only after an Entra admin grants write scopes. With write tools on, Claude can send email, manage drafts and calendar events, update mailbox settings, create and update files in OneDrive and SharePoint, and send messages in Microsoft Teams (post/reply in a channel, send a chat message, or start a new chat on the user’s behalf), always within each member’s existing Microsoft 365 permissions. Without them, the integration is read-only. Claude still can’t change Teams settings or permissions, only send messages.

Use Google Workspace connectors

Connect your Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Drive to Claude so you can search and send emails, manage your calendar, work with documents, and save files, all without leaving the conversation.

Google Workspace connectors (Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Drive) are available for all users on Claude and Claude Desktop.

Claude can edit Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides live in a pane beside the chat, on Claude on the web and Claude Desktop. You and Claude can edit the same file at the same time. See Current limitations for what isn’t supported.

For Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner or Primary Owner must enable these connectors at the organization level before individual users can authenticate. For setup instructions, read Use connectors to extend Claude’s capabilities.

What you can do

Gmail
  • Search and read emails using natural language queries
  • Draft emails with proper formatting and context
  • Send, reply to, and forward emails from Gmail. By default, outside Auto mode, Claude asks for your approval before each of these actions. On Team and Enterprise plans, owners decide whether members can allow these actions to run without asking each time.
  • Access email metadata, including attachment metadata
  • Open email attachments so Claude can read or work with the file, up to about 12 MB each. In chat, this requires code execution and file creation to be on.
  • Manage email organization with labels and threads
  • List saved drafts in your Gmail account
Google Calendar
  • View events and calendars, including shared calendars you have access to
  • Create, update, and delete events with full customization
  • Find mutual availability across attendees
  • Manage attendee lists and respond to invitations (accept, decline, or tentative)
  • Set up recurring meetings
Google Drive
  • Search and retrieve Google Docs from your Drive.
  • Share, move, and trash files in Google Drive. By default, outside Auto mode, Claude asks for your approval before each of these actions. On Team and Enterprise plans, owners decide whether members can allow these actions to run without asking each time.
  • Look up file metadata and preview directly without searching first.
  • Read Sheets, Slides, PDFs, images, and MS Office files.
  • Upload any file type, with optional auto-convert to Google formats.
  • Create folders.
  • Add Google Docs directly to chats and projects by pasting URLs or selecting from recent documents.
  • View file permissions and list recent changes to your Drive.
  • Save Claude-generated files directly to your Drive (requires code execution and file creation to be enabled).

Note: When Claude reads a Google Drive file, it extracts text content only. Images embedded in documents are not processed.

Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides
  • Edit files live in a pane beside the chat. You and Claude can work in the same file at the same time.
  • Create new Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides files.
  • Read and work with comments and suggestions in Google Docs.

These are separate connectors from Google Drive. Google Drive still handles searching, uploading, and sharing files.

How to use the connectors

Ask Claude a question that requires access to your Gmail, Calendar, or Drive. Claude automatically detects which tools it needs and uses them to respond. By default, outside Auto mode, each action Claude takes on your behalf requires your explicit approval. In Auto mode, these actions can run without asking you, unless an automated check flags them as risky or your organization requires approval. The check can miss risky actions. To approve them yourself, use Manual or set the tool’s permission to “Always ask” if that option is available. On Team and Enterprise plans, owners decide whether members can allow certain actions to run without asking each time.

Claude’s response includes citations indicating which emails, calendar events, or documents were used as sources, with links to the originals when available. You can ask follow-up questions to dig deeper into any source.

Add Google Drive files to chats
  • Click the plus sign in the chat interface.
  • Select “Add from Google Drive.”
  • Search through your recently accessed documents or paste the document’s URL.
  • When you send your message, Claude accesses and processes the document to inform its response.

You can add multiple files to a single chat to give Claude comprehensive context. The files must fit within the conversation’s context window.

Add Google Drive files to projects

The Google Drive connector is only available when adding to Files in private projects. This option will be disabled for shared projects.

  • Open your project and find the Files section.
  • Click the “+” button to add files.
  • Select “Drive.”
  • Search through your recently accessed documents or paste the document’s URL.
  • Your document is added to your project knowledge for Claude to access when chatting in that project.

Google Docs added to chats and projects sync directly from Google Drive, so you’re always working with the latest version.

Edit Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides live
  • Turn on the Docs, Sheets, and Slides connectors. Click the plus sign in the chat, hover over “Connectors,” and toggle them on. If the connector isn’t turned on when you ask Claude to edit a Google file, Claude prompts you to connect it, then continues with your request.
  • Paste a Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides link into the chat, or ask Claude to create one by name (for example, “make a Google Slides deck from these notes”). Asking for a generic “doc” or “deck” without naming Google creates a local file instead.
  • The file opens in a pane next to the conversation, and you can keep working in it while Claude edits.
    • The pane works on Claude on the web in Chrome, and on Claude Desktop when the built-in browser is turned on. If the pane isn’t available, select “Open in Google” on the file card to open the file in your regular browser.
  • Use the pane header to copy the file’s Google link or open it directly in Google.

Claude can only open and change files your Google account has access to. Your existing Google sharing permissions apply.

Each file Claude creates or edits shows as a card in the chat. Select the card to open the file in the pane, or select “Open in Google” to open it in Google. In the pane, you can copy the file’s Google link or use the share dialog.

Sign in to Google in the pane: The pane needs a Google session to show your file. On Claude on the web, it uses the Google account already signed in to your browser. On Claude Desktop, Claude asks you to sign in to Google in the pane. If the account in the pane is different from the one you connected to Claude, Claude tells you and offers to switch.

Manage individual connectors

Live editing uses separate Google Docs, Google Sheets, and Google Slides connectors alongside Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Drive. You can enable or disable specific connectors from below the chat interface:

  • Click the plus sign in the chat interface.
  • Hover over “Connectors.”
  • Toggle individual connectors on or off.

Privacy and data handling

  • You must authenticate directly with your Google account before using these connectors.
  • On Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner or Primary Owner must enable connectors at the account level before individual users can authenticate.
  • Claude can only access the Gmail, Calendar, and Drive data for the Google account you’ve connected.
  • Claude only accesses your data when you explicitly ask a question or request an action requiring this information, and retrieves the minimum information needed.
  • Claude mirrors your existing permissions—you cannot access information you don’t already have access to in Google Workspace.
  • Data retrieved while using connectors is stored on Anthropic servers, protected by Anthropic’s security infrastructure (see our Trust Center for details). This data is retained with its associated chat, so you can delete any retrieved data by deleting the chat.
  • We do not train our models on your Gmail, Drive, or Calendar connector data, ensuring your private information remains private.
    • Note: If you are using our consumer products (e.g. Claude Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, and when using Claude Code with those accounts) and you have chosen to allow us to use your chats and coding sessions for model training, then any content you copy/paste from your Gmail, Drive, Calendar, or Claude’s responses which include specific information from these connectors may be used to improve our models. For more information, refer to Is my data used for model training?
  • Data is encrypted at rest and in transit.
  • Claude Meetings (beta) also uses your Google Calendar connection, and works differently from the above. See Use Claude Meetings.
A note on Gmail permissions

During authentication, Google’s OAuth screen mentions email sending permissions. Claude can send, reply to, and forward emails, but outside Auto mode only does so with your explicit approval by default. On Team and Enterprise plans, owners decide whether members can allow these actions to run without asking each time.

Current limitations

  • Claude can’t add charts to Google Slides, and Slides edits may not appear live in the pane.
  • Live editing in the pane works on Claude on the web in Chrome and on Claude Desktop with the built-in browser turned on. In other cases, use “Open in Google” on the file card.
  • Claude can’t open a Gmail attachment over about 12 MB. Opening attachments isn’t available in every organization, or when an organization sets reading email to need approval or blocks it.
  • Some advanced Gmail filters may not be supported.
  • Complex queries may require multiple API calls.
  • Rate limits apply per Google’s API quotas.
  • Performance may vary for large mailboxes.

Troubleshooting

Reconnecting your Google account

If you see the error “Please try again. You may need to reconnect with your Google Drive account,” follow these steps:

  • Navigate to Customize > Connectors.
  • Find your Google connector and click on it to view the details.
  • Click the “Disconnect” button.
  • Click “Disconnect” in the confirmation message.
  • The next time you use a Google Workspace feature in your chat, you’ll be redirected to Google to re-authenticate.

If you’re still having trouble, disconnect from your Google account settings at myaccount.google.com/connections. Search for the Claude connection, click into the settings, and choose “Delete all connections.”

Google Workspace admin configuration

If your organization uses Google Workspace and the connectors aren’t working (you may see the message “Access blocked: your institution’s admin needs to review Claude for Google Drive”), your Google Workspace admin may need to allow Claude as a trusted application:

  • Go to admin.google.com
  • Navigate to Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage third-party app access.
  • Click “Add app,” then select “OAuth App Name.”
  • Search for “Claude” and set it as “Trusted.”
  • Wait approximately 15 minutes for Google’s policy to propagate, then try connecting again.

Live editing for Docs, Sheets, and Slides uses the same Claude for Google Drive app. Admins approve it once, and no separate approval is needed for each file type.

Frequently asked questions

What happens if I update a Google Doc after adding it to a chat?

The document continues to sync with the most up-to-date version in Google Drive.

Can I add multiple files to a single chat?

Yes. You can add multiple Google Drive files to provide Claude with comprehensive context. The documents must fit within the conversation’s context window.

What happens if I lose access to a document?

You won’t be able to view its contents in conversations where it was previously added. The document preview is removed, but the conversation history is maintained.

Does Claude have access to images, comments, or suggestions in Google Docs?

Claude can see comments and suggestions in Google Docs, but it can’t see images.

How do I get Claude to create a Google file instead of a local file?

Ask for a Google doc, Google sheet, or Google Slides deck by name, or paste a link to an existing Google file. If you ask for a document without mentioning Google, Claude creates a file you can download instead.

Can I edit the file while Claude is editing it?

Yes. You and Claude can work in the same file at the same time. Claude re-reads the current content before each change, but in a busy file, check the result.

Why does Claude ask me to sign in to Google in the pane?

The connector lets Claude change your file, and the pane needs its own Google session to show it. Sign in with the same Google account you connected to Claude.

Can Claude send emails on my behalf?

Yes. Claude can send, reply to, and forward emails from Gmail, and, outside Auto mode, asks for your approval by default before each of these actions. In Auto mode, these actions can run without asking you, unless an automated check flags them as risky or your organization requires approval. The check can miss risky actions. To approve them yourself, use Manual or set the tool’s permission to “Always ask” if that option is available. On Team and Enterprise plans, owners decide whether members can allow these actions to run without asking each time.

Can I opt out of using these connectors?

On Team and Enterprise plans, Owners and Primary Owners can disable Google Workspace connectors for their organization in Organization settings > Connectors. Individual users can also disable specific tools from the chat interface.

Browse all available connectors in the Connectors Directory.

Use interactive connectors in Claude

Interactive connectors are available for all users on Claude, Cowork, Claude Desktop, and Claude for iOS/Android. The side panel, full-site views, and opening or pinning interactive connectors from Claude’s navigation are rolling out on the web and in Claude Desktop to accounts with the new Claude experience. They aren’t available on Claude Mobile yet.

What are interactive connectors?

Some connectors can now display live, interactive apps directly within your Claude conversations. Instead of returning text-only responses, these connectors render interfaces—like analytics dashboards, task boards, or design tools—that you can interact with without leaving the chat.

For example, you might ask Claude about your project status, and instead of just describing it, Claude opens your Asana board right in the conversation. You can check off tasks, update statuses, and keep chatting with Claude—all in one place.

Some interactive connectors can also open a tool’s site in Claude. You can make changes yourself or ask Claude to make them. Each connector’s developer chooses which of these views and actions to support, so what you see varies by connector.

Claude can also generate its own custom visuals—diagrams, charts, and simple interactive elements built from scratch for your question. When a connected service offers an interactive interface that handles your request, like an MCP app, Claude will use it. Custom visuals fill the gaps when no connector interface fits what you’re asking for.

For more on Claude-generated visuals, see Custom visuals in chat.

How interactive connectors appear

Interactive connectors display in three ways:

Inline cards are compact components embedded directly in the conversation. They’re ideal for quick summaries, confirmations, and single actions—like a status update or a message draft ready to send.

Side panel keeps the interactive connector open beside your chat, so you can keep chatting and watch it update. Expand it to full screen from the panel’s title bar.

Fullscreen view provides an immersive interface for complex interactions like data visualizations, document editing, or detailed project views. The conversation input remains available so you can continue talking to Claude while interacting with the connector.

If you need to ask Claude to modify something, refine a result, or navigate to a different context, type in the conversation input—Claude can interpret your request and update the interface accordingly. Claude can only take actions the connector’s developer has made available. You approve these actions the same way you approve any connector’s actions.

Interact with connectors

You can interact directly with elements inside the connector:

  • Filter, sort, or drill into data
  • Toggle settings, check boxes, or make selections
  • Confirm and execute actions (mark complete, send, save)
  • Expand and collapse content sections
  • Ask Claude to make changes in the interactive connector you have open

If you need to ask Claude to modify something, refine a result, or navigate to a different context, type in the conversation input—Claude can interpret your request and update the interface accordingly.

Open and pin interactive connectors

You can open a supported interactive connector from Claude’s navigation without asking Claude first, and pin it to your sidebar. When an interactive connector is open full page, ask Claude about it in the box at the bottom, or work in it yourself.

Note: Pins are saved per browser, so a pin you add on the web doesn’t appear in Claude Desktop.

Which connectors are interactive?

In the Connectors Directory, connectors with this capability are marked with an “Interactive” badge. Current interactive connectors include:

  • Amplitude — View and interact with analytics dashboards
  • Asana — Manage tasks and project boards
  • Box — Work with documents and files
  • Canva — Create and edit designs
  • Clay — Manage contacts and outreach
  • Figma — Review and annotate designs
  • Hex — Explore data and notebooks
  • Slack — Draft and send messages

We’re adding support for more interactive connectors over time.

Get started with interactive connectors

  • Navigate to the Connectors Directory.
  • Look for connectors marked with the “Interactive” badge.
  • Connect and authenticate with the connector.
  • Start a conversation with Claude and ask about something the connector handles—the interactive elements will appear automatically when relevant.

Note: Interactive connectors are default on when you have the relevant connector enabled. No additional setup is needed.

Considerations for Team and Enterprise plans

Can Team and Enterprise owners control interactive connectors separately from standard connectors?

Yes. Team and Enterprise owners can disable the specific tool calls that render interactive connectors within Organization settings > Connectors. This does not disable the connector itself — text-based tool functionality continues to work normally.

Permissions and security

How are interactive connectors secured?

In-chat views run in sandboxed iframes with strict Content Security Policies. All communication between the interface and Claude uses auditable JSON-RPC messaging. Servers must predeclare which external domains they need, and the host can review HTML content before rendering.

Do interactive connectors require additional permissions beyond the connector itself?

Interactive connectors use the same permissions you granted when connecting the tool.

Who provides interactive connectors?

Third-party interactive connectors are provided by the connector’s developer, who is responsible for the content shown.

Can interactive connectors make purchases or financial transactions?

No. Purchases through a connector’s in-chat views aren’t supported.

Troubleshooting

The interface isn’t appearing
  • Check that the connector is connected and enabled for your current conversation.
  • Try starting a new conversation and asking Claude a question that the connector handles.
The connector isn’t responding to interactions
  • Check your internet connection.
  • Try refreshing the page or restarting Claude Desktop.
  • If the issue persists, disconnect and reconnect the connector in Customize > Connectors.
I want to disable interactive connectors
  • Team and Enterprise users: Ask your organization owner to disable the relevant tool calls in Organization settings > Connectors.
  • Individual users: You can disable specific connector tools via the “Search and tools” menu in your conversation.

I’m a developer. Where can I learn about building MCP Apps?

MCP Apps is the open-source extension to the Model Context Protocol that powers interactive apps. If you are building your own interactive connector, note that it must meet additional design, security, and testing requirements. For details, see Submitting to the Connectors Directory on Claude Docs.

Use Personal Finance in Claude

Personal Finance lets you link your bank, credit card, loan, and investment accounts to Claude, so you can see your balances and spending on one page and ask Claude questions about your own money. This article shows you how to set up Personal Finance, link and unlink banks, and see what Claude can access.

This feature is in beta on Pro, Max, and Ultra plans in the US only. It’s available on Claude, Claude Desktop, Claude for iOS, and Claude for Android, and it isn’t available on Free, Team, or Enterprise plans. We’re rolling it out gradually, so you might not see it yet.

Personal Finance can only read your accounts. It can’t move, manage, or invest your money. Claude uses Plaid, a network that connects apps to banks. With Plaid, you can authenticate your financial account, so Claude doesn’t ask for or see your bank password. Learn more in How your data is used.

Note: Claude is AI and can make mistakes. Learn more in How Claude answers questions about your money.

What you can do in Personal Finance

  • See your money on one page. Widgets show your spending, cash flow, accounts, subscriptions, upcoming bills, and short insights from Claude. You can add, edit, remove, and reorder them.
  • Ask Claude. Type a question on the Personal Finance page, select a suggested question, or ask in a regular chat. For example, “Where did my money go last month?” or “Which subscriptions am I paying for?”

Set up Personal Finance and link your bank

Follow these steps to set up Personal Finance and share your accounts with Claude:

  • Open Claude on the web, Claude Desktop, or the mobile app.
  • Open “Personal Finance” in the side menu. If you don’t see it, hover over More.
  • Select “Get started.”
  • Choose your goals, or skip them.
  • Select “Continue.”
  • Select “Link accounts with Plaid.”
  • On “Connect Plaid to Claude,” review what Claude will be able to access.
  • Select “Continue.”
  • In Plaid, choose your bank, sign in to it, and choose the accounts that you want to share.
  • Back in Claude, wait for your accounts to show, then select “Link another account” or “Done.”

Note: Plaid opens in a new window (web), in your default browser (Claude Desktop), inside the app (iOS), or in a browser tab (Android). Finish within 10 minutes, then return to Claude right away. Transactions can take a few minutes to sync.

Link another bank

You can link up to 16 banks. When you reach the limit, you’ll need to unlink a bank before you can link another one.

  • Web and Claude Desktop: Click “Link another account” at the top of the page.
  • iOS and Android: Tap the gear icon in the top right of the page, then tap “Link another account.”

To add an account at a linked bank, link the bank again and share every account you want Claude to read.

If Claude says the bank is already linked

Choose one of these options:

  • Switch to the new link: The new sign-in replaces the old one, and Claude reads only the accounts you shared this time. Choose this to add an account or fix a bank.
  • Keep it as it is: Claude keeps your existing link and doesn’t link anything new.
  • Keep both: Choose this for a second login at the same bank, such as a joint or business account. If an account is in both logins, Claude counts it once when your bank shows it the same way under each login. If your bank shows it differently, it may be counted twice in your totals.

What Claude can access

For the accounts you choose to share, Claude can read:

  • Bank names
  • Account names, types, and last four digits
  • Balances and credit limits
  • Up to 24 months of transactions, including the amount, date, merchant, category, and your bank’s description

Account numbers: Plaid gives Claude only the last few digits of each account number (usually four). If your bank writes a full number into an account’s name or a transaction’s description, Claude may see it there.

Investments, loans, and cards: Claude can read details of your credit cards and loans (including mortgages and student loans), such as interest rates, statement balances, last and next payments, due dates, whether a payment is overdue, and a loan’s start date, original amount, and scheduled payoff date. For a student loan, Claude can also read its status (such as in school or delinquent) and its type of repayment plan (such as income-based). For investment and retirement accounts, Claude can also read transactions, such as trades, dividends, contributions, withdrawals, fees, and taxes withheld. Additionally, Claude can read what these accounts hold, including each holding’s name, quantity, price, value, and cost. Plaid’s own screens may also ask for your consent to share investment, credit, and loan data.

How your data is used

  • Your permission: By connecting Plaid, you’re giving your permission to share certain data with Claude. The list is in the What Claude can access section above.
  • Your bank login: Claude uses Plaid to connect to your bank. You sign in through Plaid, so Claude doesn’t ask for or see your bank password.
  • How Claude uses your financial data: We use this data to respond to your requests. When you chat with Claude in the Personal Finance hub, those conversations aren’t used to train our models. For anything you share with Claude outside the hub, your privacy settings apply. The data appears in your conversation and stays in your chat history until you delete the chat, subject to our data retention practices. The service providers that host Claude for us also handle bank data. Plaid handles it under its own terms and privacy policy.
  • How to stop: Unlink a bank, and Claude stops reading it (see Unlink a bank). You can also disconnect Claude at my.plaid.com.

For more information, see the Anthropic Privacy Policy and the Plaid Privacy Policy. Learn more about our data handling and retention.

How Claude answers questions about your money

  • What Claude reads: Claude uses Plaid to read data from your linked accounts, such as balances and transactions (see What Claude can access above). It uses that data to answer your questions about your money.
  • Personal Finance can only read your accounts. It can’t move, manage, or invest your money.
  • Claude is AI and can make mistakes. Check important figures against your bank’s own app or statements. Learn more about incorrect or misleading responses.
  • A figure can differ from your bank’s. Balances can be a day or two old. An account you link through two logins may be counted twice. While Claude can’t read a bank, the page’s spending figures leave that bank out, so a budget can show more money left than you have.

Personal Finance helps you understand your money, and it isn’t designed to give investment advice.

Use your accounts in chats

  • Claude reads your linked accounts without asking each time, unless you change that (see Turn Plaid off or on for chats below). It asks before it links or unlinks a bank in a chat.
  • Once Claude has used your accounts in a chat, it’s designed not to save anything from that chat to memory or search that chat later. It also leaves it out of your monthly recap, including the title. In that chat, Claude can still show text and tables and make plain text files, such as .csv files. It may not be able to run code or work with Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or PDF files.
  • Claude asks before it publishes an artifact from a chat that used your linked accounts. The artifact may include data from your bank accounts. It stays until you delete it, even if you delete the chat.
  • A shared chat link shows your messages and Claude’s replies, including any figures from your accounts. It can also show a chart or artifact that Claude made.
  • Artifacts can read the linked accounts of the person who opens them, if that person has Personal Finance and allows Plaid. Any figures in an artifact, including saved ones, are shown to everyone who opens it.

Turn Plaid off or on for chats

  • Web and Claude Desktop: Click “+” in the message box, click “Connectors,” then switch Plaid off or on.
  • iOS and Android: Tap “+” next to the message box, then “Connectors,” then “Plaid.” Under “All tools” (on Android, “Set all tools”), choose “Blocked” to turn Plaid off or “Always allow” to turn it back on. With “Needs approval,” Claude asks before each read, unless the chat is set to “Automatically approve.” Your choice also applies to new chats.

Sign in again to a bank

Banks sometimes end Claude’s access. The bank then shows “Sign-in expired” or “Claude’s access to this bank has ended.” To restore access:

  • Navigate to Personal Finance.
  • Open your linked accounts. On the web and Claude Desktop, click the three-dot menu (“…”) at the top of the page, then click “Manage linked accounts.” On iOS and Android, tap the gear icon.
  • Select “Sign in again” on the bank.
  • Sign in with the same bank login you used to link it.

When it works, you see “Claude can read [bank] again” and your dashboard stays as it was.

Unlink a bank

Follow these steps to unlink a bank:

  • Navigate to Personal Finance.
  • Open your linked accounts. On the web and Claude Desktop, click the three-dot menu (“…”) at the top of the page, then click “Manage linked accounts.” On iOS and Android, tap the gear icon.
  • Select “Unlink” on the bank. On iOS and Android, tap the bank first to open it.
  • Select “Unlink” again to confirm.

When you unlink a bank:

  • Claude stops reading your accounts at this bank.
  • Every account you linked with that bank login is unlinked. You can’t unlink a single account.
  • What Claude already said stays in your chats, and in any artifacts or shared links until you remove them. You can link the bank again later.

Important: If it’s your last linked bank, your dashboard resets too. Your widgets, their settings (such as budgets), and your setup answers are deleted, and this can’t be undone.

Stop using Personal Finance

To stop using Personal Finance, unlink every bank:

  • Navigate to Personal Finance.
  • On the web and Claude Desktop, click the three-dot menu (“…”) at the top of the page, then click “Manage linked accounts.” On iOS and Android, tap the gear icon.
  • Select “Unlink all banks.”

You can also disconnect Claude at my.plaid.com, Plaid’s own site for your connections. Learn more in Plaid’s steps.

If you lose a device, log it out. Learn more about managing your active sessions.

If your plan ends or you delete your account

When your paid plan ends, you can’t open Personal Finance, and Claude can’t read your accounts in chats. Your banks stay linked until you unlink them.

  • Before your plan ends: Unlink your banks if you don’t plan to come back.
  • If you subscribe again: Your banks and dashboard are as you left them. A bank may ask you to sign in again.
  • If you move to a Team or Enterprise organization: Claude unlinks your banks when you start the move.

Unlink your banks after your plan has ended

  • On the web, click “Customize” in the sidebar. If you see “Plugins” instead, go to claude.ai/customize/connectors/yours and skip step 2.
  • Click “Connectors,” then click “Yours.”
  • If “Plaid” is listed, open it, click the button that starts with “Unlink,” and confirm.
  • If “Plaid” isn’t listed, disconnect Claude at my.plaid.com or contact Support. Learn more in Plaid’s steps.

If you plan to delete your Claude account

When you delete your account, Claude unlinks your banks automatically. This happens after the deletion is processed.

Current limitations

  • You can link US banks only.
  • Claude can’t use your linked accounts in scheduled tasks, Cowork tasks, or Claude Code, and may not be able to use them in a project.
  • Personal Finance isn’t available in Claude Duet.
  • Data exports don’t yet include your saved Personal Finance dashboard.

Troubleshooting

What you see

What to do

No “Personal Finance” in the sidebar or side menu

Check your plan, use your personal account (not a Team or Enterprise account), and update the app. Outside the US, or on a VPN that connects from another country, Personal Finance doesn’t appear until you’re back (your banks stay linked). It may also not be on for your account yet.

“Nothing new was linked.” or “[Bank] is already linked.”

Claude found no new account. To add one, link the bank again, and in Plaid share that account and every other account you want Claude to read.

A link from Claude Desktop or Android fails

Finish in the browser that Claude opened, and don’t reload Plaid’s page. From Claude Desktop, that browser must be signed in to Claude with the same account.

You linked a bank, but it isn’t in your linked accounts

Wait a minute or two, then open Personal Finance again. If the bank still isn’t there, Claude didn’t save it. Link the bank again, finish within 10 minutes, don’t close Plaid yourself, and return to Claude right away.

Transactions are missing

A new bank can take a few minutes to sync. If the bank asks for a new sign-in, select “Sign in again.” If nothing has loaded a day after you linked the bank, link it again (if Claude asks, choose “Switch to the new link”) or wait for the bank.

“Claude can’t read this bank.”

Don’t unlink it first. Link the bank again with “Link another account.” If Claude asks, choose “Switch to the new link” (or “Keep both” if that isn’t offered). If the old entry is still listed afterward, unlink it then. The one exception: if you already have 16 banks, unlink this bank first, then link it again.

Claude doesn’t use your accounts in a chat

On iOS or Android, update the app. Then ask Claude to use your linked accounts, and check that Plaid is on. You can also start a new chat outside of a project: a chat that already ran code or made files, or that started from an artifact, can’t use your accounts. If it still doesn’t work in the app, go to claude.ai in a browser and start a new chat with the same account.

Get help

On the web, click your initials or name in the lower left corner, then click “Get help.” Learn how to get support.

Important: Don’t share your bank login or full account numbers with anyone, including Support.

Use the GitHub integration

Connect your GitHub repositories directly to Claude to provide comprehensive context for your software development tasks. You can easily add repositories by selecting them from a list, helping Claude better understand and assist with your codebase.

For more information on enabling GitHub within your account, see Use connectors to extend Claude’s capabilities.

How to add GitHub repositories

Note: If you’re currently unauthenticated with GitHub, you’ll be redirected to GitHub to authenticate before you can use this integration.

Chats
  • Click the “+” button on the lower left corner of the chat interface.
  • Select “Add from GitHub” from the drop-down.
  • Use the file browser to select specific files and folders.
  • When you send your message, Claude will access and process the content to inform its response.
Projects
  • Click the “+” button in the upper right corner of your project knowledge section.
  • Select “GitHub” from the drop-down.
  • Search through your accessible repositories, or paste a repository URL.
  • Use the file browser to select specific files and folders.
  • Your selected content will be added to the project knowledge for Claude to access and process.
  • You can use the “Sync” icon to ensure you’re working with the most up-to-date version of your codebase.
  • You can use the “Configure files” icon to modify which files and folders Claude analyzes.

Connect to private repositories

  • If Claude cannot access a repository after you enter a valid URL, it most likely means you’re attempting to connect Claude to a private repository: Follow the link to our GitHub App, where you can grant access to repos if you’re a GitHub administrator, or send a request to your GitHub organization’s administrators.
  • Grant access yourself if you can: You can choose between letting Claude access all repos or specific ones.
  • Request access if you don’t have the necessary permissions: The administrators of your GitHub organization will receive an email notification about your request. Once they approve the request, you’ll be able to sync and access the repository in Claude.

Best practices

  • Start small: Begin by selecting a small subset of your codebase to analyze. This will help you get familiar with how Claude interprets and discusses your code.
  • Iterate and refine: If Claude’s initial response doesn’t fully address your question, don’t hesitate to ask follow-up questions or request clarification.
  • Combine with human expertise: Use Claude’s insights as a starting point for further investigation and discussion with your team. Please review Claude’s work.
  • Thoughtful file selection: When using “Configure files,” be strategic about your selections. Include key files and directories that are central to your current task or project, but avoid selecting unnecessary files to keep within token limits and maintain focus.
  • Regular updates: Remember to refresh your project’s GitHub sync periodically to ensure Claude is working with the most up-to-date version of your codebase and especially before starting a new analysis or when you know there have been significant changes to your repo.

Troubleshooting

Repositories from an organization don’t appear after connecting

If your GitHub connection shows as connected but private repositories from a specific organization don’t appear, that organization may require single sign-on (SSO). When SSO is required, each user must separately authorize the Claude app for that organization. Until you do, GitHub filters that organization’s private repositories from your view, even though your connection is otherwise working.

When Claude detects this state, the repository picker shows a banner prompting you to authorize SSO. To authorize the Claude app for your organization:

  • Go to github.com/settings/applications and open the Claude entry.
  • Under Organization access, click “Grant” next to the relevant GitHub organization.
  • If the button reads “Request” instead of “Grant,” you don’t have permission to authorize the app yourself. A GitHub organization admin must approve your request from the organization’s OAuth application policy settings.

Important: Disconnecting and reconnecting GitHub in your Claude settings won’t fix this. A fresh connection doesn’t automatically authorize organizations that require SSO, so you’ll need to complete the authorization steps above.

If your organization uses GitHub Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users (EMU), connect GitHub while you’re signed in with your managed account and have an active SSO session. An organization owner can check the Claude app under Settings > Third-party Access > GitHub Apps in your GitHub organization, and confirm that it has access to the repositories you need and has no pending permission requests.

Can’t link GitHub to an organization with zero data retention

If your organization has zero data retention (ZDR) enabled for Claude Code, you can’t link the Claude GitHub App to your Claude organization. This is a restriction of ZDR, not a GitHub permissions problem: linking requires Anthropic to store your organization’s GitHub connection, which ZDR doesn’t allow.

When you try to link GitHub in Organization settings > Git providers, you may see an error saying you need to be an owner of the GitHub organization, even if you already are one.

Important: Changing roles or app permissions on GitHub, or disconnecting and reconnecting GitHub, won’t fix this. Contribution metrics in Claude Code analytics aren’t available to ZDR organizations for the same reason.

If your organization needs GitHub linking, contact your Anthropic account team to discuss your ZDR configuration. Learn more about zero data retention for Claude Code.

Frequently asked questions

What information is retrieved from GitHub?

Only files (names and contents) in a repo on a specific branch are synced. We do not retrieve commit history, PRs, or other metadata.

What happens if my repository is updated after adding it to a project?

You can click “Sync now” to fetch the latest changes from your repository. This will update all previously selected files and folders.

Can I add multiple repositories to a single project or chat?

Yes, you can add multiple repositories to provide Claude with comprehensive context for your development tasks. The repositories must fit within Claude’s context window.

What happens if I lose access to a repository?

If you lose access to a repository, you won’t be able to view its contents in projects where it was previously added. The repository preview will be removed, though the conversation history will be maintained.

Browse all available connectors in the Connectors Directory.

Conversation management

Claude Haiku 4.5 was removed from the model selector

On October 29, 2026, we removed Claude Haiku 4.5 from the model selector in chat, Claude Cowork, and Claude Design on the Free, Pro, and Max plans, including in Claude Desktop and Claude Mobile. Claude Haiku 5.5 replaced it. This article explains what changed, where Haiku 4.5 is still available, and what happened to your existing chats.

What changed and when

We announced this change on October 15, 2026. As of October 29, 2026, you can no longer select Haiku 4.5 under “More models” in the model selector. If it was your selected model, Claude switched you to Haiku 5.5.

Where Haiku 4.5 is still available

This change didn’t affect Haiku 4.5 in:

  • Claude Code
  • Team and Enterprise plans
  • Claude Platform (API)

What happened to your existing chats

Your Haiku 4.5 chats are still in your account, and nothing was deleted. When you continue one after October 29, Claude responds using Haiku 5.5. You can switch to a different model at any time.

To keep a copy of your chats, you can export your data at any time. Learn more about exporting your Claude data.

Switch models in a chat

You can change the model at any point in a chat. The change applies starting with Claude’s next response.

  • Click the model name next to the send button.
  • Choose a model, or click “More models” to see additional options.

Learn more about changing the model, effort, and thinking settings.

Delete or rename a conversation
