  • Your cloud provider bills you. You pay for the tokens you use, and there are no seat licenses. See the feature comparison.
  • Your provider determines who processes your data. On Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud, the cloud provider processes conversation data in the region or routing option you choose, and the app doesn’t send user data, prompts, or completions to Anthropic. On Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic operates the Claude models as an independent processor for Microsoft. Some models add their own data retention and data sharing requirements. See Compare cloud providers.

You can run Claude Enterprise and Claude Desktop on 3P side by side during the move. Claude Desktop on 3P keeps its application data in a separate directory, so the two can coexist on one computer. They share a few folders, such as ~/Claude/ and ~/.claude/. If you need to go back later, see Migrate Claude Desktop from a cloud provider to Claude Enterprise.

Most of this guide applies to every provider. For details specific to Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Foundry, see Compare cloud providers.

Note: Settings and version requirements change between releases. Check the linked page before you change a setting.

What moves and what doesn’t

The import brings over each user’s own chats and projects, plus any Cowork and Code sessions already on their computer. Plan to move everything else by hand before your cutoff date, which is the last day users can access work in claude.ai. You set this date.

The import is a one-time copy. It doesn’t stay in sync with claude.ai, but you can run it again to pick up newer chats without creating duplicates.

Item

Does the import bring it over?

What to do

Each user’s own chats

Yes

Run the import. Run it again on your cutoff date to pick up newer chats.

Each user’s own projects and project instructions

Yes. The user reviews and accepts the instructions before they take effect.

Check each project after the import. If a project with the same name already exists, choose “Merge into existing” or “Keep separate.”

Project knowledge files and chat attachments

No. A user’s export never includes file contents. Chats keep the messages that mention a file, but not the file itself.

Gather the original files and add them back to the project in Claude Desktop. The Primary Owner’s organization export is the only export that includes file contents. It doesn’t include Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or PDF files that Claude created. Keep it as an archive.

Cowork and Claude Code sessions already on the computer

Yes, in the Cowork & Code step. Sessions are copied, not moved.

Choose how far back to go. This step isn’t available if you limit import to specific organizations.

Cowork and Code sessions in the cloud

No. The wizard imports only sessions on the computer.

Finish or download the work before your cutoff date.

Other users’ content

No. The import brings over the user’s own data only. Other users’ content isn’t included.

If users rely on a project that someone else created, ask its creator to import it. See Replace shared projects.

Memory

An export contains the user’s memory, but the import brings over chats and projects.

Copy it by hand. See Move memory by hand.

Personal instructions

Plan to move these by hand.

Copy the text from Instructions for Claude (called Instructions in the newer Settings layout) in claude.ai settings.

Artifacts

Partly. The final version of artifacts Claude created in a conversation comes over as an output file. Earlier versions don’t, and a size limit applies.

Export or download the ones you need.

Files Claude created

Partly. The final version of files written with Claude’s file-creation tool comes over as an output file. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files aren’t in exports.

Download them from the conversation.

Skills users built

Plan to move these by hand.

Download them from Customize > Skills. Admins can share skills with everyone through a plugin marketplace.

Connectors

No. They’re part of the new configuration.

Admins set them up as managed MCP servers.

Audit logs

No

An Owner or Primary Owner can export the past 180 days before you close the organization. If you use customer-managed encryption keys, use the Compliance API instead.

Claude Code CLI settings, memory, and local sessions

No need. Each developer’s own settings, memory, and local sessions already live on the computer. Organization-managed settings and skills synced from claude.ai work differently.

Leave them in place. See Move Claude Code CLI users.

Custom roles and model access settings

No. They’re set in your Claude Enterprise organization.

Set them up again at your provider and in the new configuration. See Plan for restricted models and access programs.

Note: Primary Owners don’t see the personal “Export data” button. Use your pilot to test how the Primary Owner’s own history will move.

Important: Content that a user has deleted, or that your retention settings have removed, isn’t included in any export. Check your retention period before you set your timeline.

Replace shared projects

In Claude Desktop on 3P, projects live on each user’s computer and aren’t shared with other users. To give a team the same starting point, we recommend the following:

  • Shared instructions and reference material: Package them as a skill or plugin and distribute it to everyone. See Distribute skills and plugins.
  • Shared files: Keep them in the file sharing or repository tools you already use. Claude writes artifacts and scheduled-task results to ~/Claude/ in the user’s home directory. In Cowork sessions, files that Claude creates in a project are saved in the project’s folders.
Move memory by hand

In claude.ai, each user can ask Claude to write out their memories and copy the text. They then paste what they want to keep into one of these places in Claude Desktop:

  • Global instructions: Go to Settings > Cowork and click “Edit” next to Global instructions. They’re included in every session.
  • Project instructions: Add the text to a project’s instructions. They apply to every session in that project.

Set up the import tools

Claude Desktop includes tools for this move, and most are off until an admin turns them on. We recommend the latest Claude Desktop release.

Turn on import

Both of these settings must be on before users can import history from your Claude Enterprise organization. Both are off by default.

  • In claude.ai: Have an Owner or Primary Owner go to Organization settings > Data and privacy and turn on Allow members to export their own data.
  • In Claude Desktop: Turn on the import wizard. In the Enterprise Admin Console, go to Capabilities > Claude.ai data import and turn on Enable import. With MDM or a bootstrap server, set enabled to true under claudeAiImport.

Users then go to Settings > Import & export and click “Import…” to open the import wizard.

Optional settings and tools

Tool

What it does

How to use it

Import prompt

Prompts users to import when they start a new chat or task, so they don’t have to find the setting.

Set bannerBehavior under claudeAiImport to off (the default), detect, or show.

Organization allowlist

Limits import to the claude.ai organizations you list, by sign-in only. Personal accounts are refused. Import from a file or from earlier local sessions is turned off. Automatic import of earlier third-party sessions isn’t affected.

Set allowedOrganizationUuids under claudeAiImport. Requires 2.26454.0 or later.

Rollout by group

Turns on Claude.ai data import for one group at a time. If a user is in several groups, only the highest-ranked policy that sets it applies.

Use permission policies in the console.

Automatic import of earlier third-party sessions

For computers that already ran Claude Desktop on 3P under an earlier configuration, such as a pilot on MDM that moves to the console. It runs once per computer, in the background, and brings over local data such as sessions, projects, and memory. It doesn’t bring over claude.ai history, which still needs the wizard.

On by default in Enterprise Admin Console organizations, under Capabilities > Claude.ai data import > Automatically import earlier third-party sessions. Elsewhere, it runs only if an organization ID is configured and an admin sets automatic3pImport.

Session export

Saves a user’s Claude Desktop data, such as sessions, projects, memory, scheduled tasks, skills, and uploaded plugins, to an unencrypted zip file. The wizard on another device with the same operating system and organization can import it, unless you limit import to specific organizations. Both devices need 4.23118.0 or later. It doesn’t include Claude Code CLI sessions.

Set exportEnabled under claudeAiImport. It has no effect unless enabled is also true.

Import event in your telemetry

Logs desktop_claude_ai_import for each claude.ai history import. For sign-in imports, it names the source organization. Use it to count who has imported.

Requires OpenTelemetry export to your collector with otlpDesktopLogLevel set to info, on 2.26454.0 or later.

Note: While a user signs in and fetches an export, the wizard needs access to claude.ai, hcaptcha.com, *.hcaptcha.com, api.anthropic.com, and storage.googleapis.com. Importing a downloaded export file needs none of them. Keep these hosts open until your cutoff date. If you use the console, all but storage.googleapis.com stay required for it.

With MDM or a bootstrap server, auto-updates and other features can also use claude.ai and api.anthropic.com, so check Telemetry and egress before you close them.

Important: In a HIPAA-ready organization, member data export can’t be turned on, so users can’t import claude.ai chats or projects. If you don’t limit import to specific organizations, they can still import Cowork and Claude Code sessions already on their computer.

Checklist for users

Share this checklist with each wave of users before they move. For the full walkthrough, see Import history from claude.ai.

Before you move, in claude.ai

  • Download any Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF files Claude created for you, and export any artifacts you need in another format.
  • Gather the original files you uploaded to projects and chats. They don’t come over.
  • Copy your memory and your Instructions for Claude (called Instructions in the newer Settings layout) into a local file.
  • Download the skills you built from Customize > Skills.
  • Make a note of the connectors you use, so you can ask for any that are missing.

On the day you move, in Claude Desktop

  • Open Claude Desktop and sign in the way your IT team described.
  • Go to Settings > Import & export and click “Import…” to open the wizard.
  • Click “Sign in to claude.ai…” and, in the browser, choose your work organization and click “Authorize.”
  • Return to Claude Desktop and click “Fetch export,” then “Continue.”
  • Choose how far back to include local sessions in the Cowork & Code step, or skip the step.
  • Click “Import” in the Review step.
  • If a Duplicates step appears, choose “Merge into existing” or “Keep separate” for each project.

After the import

  • Open each imported project. Review and accept its instructions, then add your files back. To use a project’s folder in Chat, add the folder to the project again.
  • Open an imported chat and send a message. Click “Trust and resume” when asked.
  • Paste your saved memory and instructions into Claude Desktop.
  • Reconnect the connectors you use.
  • Run the import once more on your organization’s cutoff date to pick up newer chats. It won’t create duplicates.

What changes for users

Most day-to-day work stays the same. Chat, Cowork, projects, artifacts, memory, scheduled tasks, file upload, skills, plugins, connectors, and Code are all features of Claude Desktop on 3P. The main differences are where work is stored and what admins control. Voice mode, Claude Security, and Claude Tag aren’t available, and Claude in Chrome works only with the Enterprise Admin Console.

Area

What changes

What to tell users

Where users work

There’s no mobile or claude.ai web access. Claude runs in the desktop app only. Cowork needs macOS 14 or later, or Windows 10 build 19041 or later.

Use Claude Desktop on your work computer. After your cutoff date, you won’t have the Claude mobile apps or claude.ai.

Sign-in

With per-user sign-in, users sign in inside the app through AWS IAM Identity Center, Google or Workforce Identity, or Microsoft Entra ID. With the Enterprise Admin Console, users sign in with their work email, restart, then sign in to the provider.

Expect a new sign-in screen, and expect to sign in again occasionally.

History

It’s stored on the device. Except for SSH remote sessions and any export or copy that was made, it exists only on that device, so deleted history can’t be recovered.

Your history doesn’t follow you to another computer. Talk to IT before you change devices.

Sharing

Sharing between users isn’t available.

Share the output file instead of a link to the chat or project.

Long tasks and scheduled tasks

Sessions are local. The device must be awake to run long processes and scheduled tasks.

Keep your computer on and awake while a task runs.

Memory and search

Memory is stored on the device. Chat-history search and nightly summaries aren’t available in Chat.

In Chat, Claude won’t search your past chats.

Imported chats

When a user sends the first message in an imported chat, the app asks them to confirm. The reply then comes from your configured provider, not from claude.ai.

Click “Trust and resume” to continue.

Web search and fetch

Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry offer native search. Amazon Bedrock doesn’t, so you add a search provider. In Chat and Cowork, fetch reaches only the hosts you allow.

Search may look different, and Claude may only be able to open approved sites.

Note: Unified Claude combines Chat and Cowork into one experience. It’s on by default in current versions of Claude Desktop, even if you turned Cowork off earlier. Turning it off turns off both Chat and Cowork. Code isn’t affected. Where your earlier settings leave only Code on, the newest versions keep it that way until December 17, 2026. Base your screenshots and training on the Unified Claude layout.

What changes for admins

You take on more after the move. You’re now responsible for the cloud account, the device configuration, cost controls, and monitoring.

Task

How it works in Claude Desktop on 3P

Where you manage settings

Choose the web-based Enterprise Admin Console, an MDM profile, or a bootstrap server.

Identity and groups

In the console, you add users and groups, connect SSO and SCIM, and set permission policies for each group. With MDM or a bootstrap server, you manage access through those tools and your cloud provider’s identity tools. See Plan identity and sign-in.

Model access

Model settings and custom roles in your Claude Enterprise organization stay there, so you set model access again in the new configuration. The model picker comes from inferenceModels, and a console policy can narrow it for each group. See Plan for restricted models and access programs.

Cost control

There are no seats and no claude.ai spend limits. In the app, inferenceMaxTokensPerWindow limits each user’s tokens per window on each device. It has no effect unless inferenceTokenWindowHours is also set. Cached tokens don’t count, so it doesn’t cap your provider’s bill. Budgets, alerts, and quotas come from your cloud provider.

Usage reporting by user or team

Per-user sign-in gives each user an identity at the provider. Shared keys don’t. Cost attribution tools differ by provider. The console has optional usage analytics, which is off by default.

Monitoring and audit

OpenTelemetry export to your own collector covers many capabilities of the Compliance API and Analytics API. It sends metadata only by default. Metadata includes the user’s identity and the paths of connected folders. If you turn on skill scanning, a scan summary can quote the skill. You can opt in to prompt and tool content, which goes only to your collector. With the console, you can also turn on the Compliance API to record administrator activity. It starts recording in every organization under the same parent organization, so check what it captures first.

Decide what to capture before rollout. An LLM gateway sees model requests and responses, but not session events recorded on the device, such as permission decisions. To include the shell commands Claude runs in the export, add toolDetails to otlpContentCapture. Long commands are shortened. Your receiver must accept OTLP over HTTP in both protobuf and JSON. If your monitoring platform accepts only its own format, run an OpenTelemetry Collector that forwards to it.

Claude Code CLI policy

Server-managed settings don’t apply on a cloud provider. Deliver policy by file, macOS profile, or Windows registry. See Move Claude Code CLI users.

For network hosts, updates, retention on devices, and what the app sends to Anthropic, see Installation and setup, Telemetry and egress, and User identity and local data.

Distribute skills and plugins

In Claude Desktop on 3P, you distribute skills and plugins through your configuration. For full details, see MCP, plugins, skills, and hooks.

Use a plugin marketplace (recommended): Host a marketplace in git or over HTTPS and point to it with allowedPluginMarketplaces. You roll out updates by changing one configuration value instead of pushing files to every device. You can also set this in the console.

Review web search and web fetch

Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry support native search. On Google Cloud, an organization policy turns it off by default, so allow it there first. Amazon Bedrock doesn’t, so you add a search provider. In Cowork and Chat, web fetch reaches only the hosts you list in coworkEgressAllowedHosts. In Code, that list doesn’t block fetches to other hosts. For who sees search queries, and how to limit, log, or turn off search, see Web search and web fetch.

Test web search before rollout on each operating system and each network your users work from, such as the office and home. If you add a search provider, its host must be reachable through your firewall and proxy. The app can’t prompt for a proxy username and password. If your proxy requires sign-in, such as with NTLM, plan extra testing. You may need a local forwarding proxy on each device that signs in to yours. Another option is a remote MCP search server that you host.

To learn how we approach prompt injection, see Mitigating the risk of prompt injections in browser use, How we contain Claude across products, and the Security page in the Claude Code docs. For security documents in the Trust Center, see the Security posture section of the overview.

Read these if they apply to you:

  • Move Claude Code CLI users: For organizations whose developers use the Claude Code CLI. It covers how policy reaches each device, what carries over, and a checklist for developers.
  • Plan identity and sign-in: Every sign-in your users will see, and what to do if you’re also changing identity providers (IdPs).
  • Plan for restricted models and access programs: For organizations in the Cyber Verification Program or another access program, or that use custom roles to limit models.
  • Compare cloud providers: How Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry differ on data handling, sign-in, web search, and public sector needs.

Decisions to make before your pilot

These choices set your configuration and what users experience. Start with these four, because they affect the pilot most.

Decision

Options

What to consider

  1. Which provider to use

Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or your own LLM gateway

Your existing cloud agreements and identity setup, who processes conversation data, native web search, data residency options, and public sector needs. Compare them in Compare cloud providers.

  1. How configuration reaches devices

Enterprise Admin Console, MDM, or a bootstrap server

Choose this early, and evaluate the console first. You don’t run a server or push a profile for each change.

Console: It gives you SSO, SCIM, policies for each group, and Claude in Chrome. It needs api.anthropic.com at every launch, and users hold an Anthropic account for sign-in. Sign-in also needs claude.ai, hcaptcha.com, and *.hcaptcha.com. If a device can’t reach api.anthropic.com at launch, the app can’t connect to your provider until it can. The inference connection applies to the whole organization.

MDM: It doesn’t need api.anthropic.com to get its configuration, or an Anthropic account to sign in, though other features can use that host. Settings for different groups mean separate profiles. Each change means pushing an updated profile. If another team runs your MDM, agree on how quickly it can deploy one.

Bootstrap server: You host and run it. If it’s unreachable when the app launches, the app has no inference provider until it recovers, so run it across multiple replicas or regions.

Your own tool: If you build a tool to deliver settings, you also maintain and version it. If it writes to the local configuration file, users can edit those settings.

In all cases: Deliver your main configuration one way per device. On Claude Desktop 2.37337.0 or later, a user who signs in to any organization that uses the console can move a device off a managed profile. To prevent that, set deploymentMode to 3p in the profile (devices before 4.16336.0 also need disableDeploymentModeChooser). To allow only your organization, set forceLoginOrgUUID, which can be used alongside the console.

  1. How users authenticate to the provider

Per-user sign-in inside the app, a credential helper, your own authenticating proxy or gateway, or a shared key

Per-user sign-in gives each user an identity at the provider. Shared keys (bearer token, service account key, API key) are for a proof of concept with a single team. See the setup guide for Bedrock, Google Cloud, or Foundry. The console doesn’t offer static keys or bearer tokens.

  1. What users can import

Open import, or allowedOrganizationUuids set to your organization’s ID

With the list set, users import by sign-in only, and only from the organizations you list. Personal accounts are refused. Import from a file and from earlier sessions on the computer is turned off. The list needs Claude Desktop 2.26454.0 or later, and earlier releases ignore it. Decide whether users who used personal accounts for work should bring that history in.

Then settle the rest:

  • Which parts of the app each group gets: Unified Claude, which combines Chat and Cowork, and Code.
  • Which permission modes users get. Agree on this with your security team before rollout. If users must approve every action, they may start to approve without reading, so decide which actions need a prompt. Decide on Auto mode, which new Code sessions normally start in unless you turn it off, bypass permissions mode, and which tools always ask.
  • How web search works. See Review web search and web fetch.
  • How to control cost: the in-app token cap, plus your provider’s budgets, alerts, and quotas.
  • What telemetry to send to Anthropic and to your own collector.
  • How to handle data on devices: retention and legal hold, and session export for device changes. For a legal hold, set the chat, Cowork, and Code retention periods to 3650 days for the users on hold. The sessionRetentionHold setting stops working on December 17, 2026.
  • How to configure Claude Code CLI users.
  • When to make any IdP change: before the first wave moves, between waves, or after the last import.
  • What to do about restricted models and access programs: turn them on for the cloud account, keep some Claude Enterprise seats for that work, or stop using them.

Plan your move

We recommend moving in waves, one set of users at a time, with an overlap period when both Claude Enterprise and Claude Desktop on 3P are running. Set a clear cutoff date, and give each user a short checklist to finish before they move. Keep claude.ai available until the last wave has imported.

Phase 1: Plan for migration

Who’s involved: AI program lead, IT, and your Anthropic account team

  • Make the choices listed in Decisions to make before your pilot.
  • Name one owner each for the cloud account, device management, identity, network, and communications and training.
  • List what’s in your Claude Enterprise organization: users, shared projects, skills your organization provides, and connectors in use.
  • List the users who rely on the Claude mobile apps or on claude.ai in a browser, such as executives who work from a phone or tablet. Claude Desktop on 3P has neither, so decide whether those users keep Claude Enterprise seats.
  • Agree on how you’ll measure success, the order of your waves, and your cutoff date for claude.ai.
  • Count who uses the Claude Code CLI. Note the server-managed settings, cloud sessions, and claude.ai connectors they depend on.
  • List every sign-in your users will see, and note any IdP change planned for the same period. See Plan identity and sign-in.
  • List the access programs, restricted models, and custom roles you use today. See Plan for restricted models and access programs.
Phase 2: Set up the new environment

Who’s involved: cloud, device management, network, and identity admins

  • Enable or deploy the models with your provider, grant the inference role, and request enough quota for your users. Follow your provider’s setup guide, linked in Compare cloud providers.
  • Connect your IdP to the cloud provider and test sign-in with a small group.
  • Run the Cowork readiness check on each hardware model. Cowork needs hardware virtualization and, on Windows, the Virtual Machine Platform feature.
  • Package the app and test automated deployment with the team that manages your devices. Allow time for this work. On Windows, use the .msix package, which Cowork requires. Installing it needs administrator rights.
  • Build the configuration in the console, or build it in the app and export it for MDM. Plan for the latest Claude Desktop release on every device.
  • Decide which settings users shouldn’t change, and set each one before the first user signs in. For example, Code offers Auto mode unless you set autoModeEnabled to false. Deliver these settings from the console, an MDM profile, or a bootstrap server, because users can edit the local configuration file. The console alone doesn’t keep a device on your settings. To enforce them, also deploy forceLoginOrgUUID in a machine-level managed profile. The key limits which organizations users can sign in to in Claude Desktop, so list your Enterprise Admin Console organization and every other organization they still need during the overlap period. Then check on a test device which settings users can still change. With MDM, confirm that the in-app configuration window opens read-only. On Windows, a misspelled value also locks the window, so compare each value in the diagnostic report’s managed-config.txt with the value you set.
  • Open the required network hosts, and allow the app in your endpoint security tools by its signing identity.
  • Configure connectors, the plugin marketplace, web search, the banner, the token cap, and OpenTelemetry export.
  • Set up model access rules at the provider and in the app’s model list.
  • Set budget alerts with your provider, and turn on cost attribution before the first user signs in.
  • For CLI users, deploy Claude Code managed settings with the provider variables, pinned models, model limits, and allowedProviders. See Move Claude Code CLI users.
  • If you hold an access program grant, link the cloud account in the Verification Portal and turn on access. Allow for the lead time.
Phase 3: Prepare your existing users

Who’s involved: Owner, Primary Owner, and communications lead

  • Turn on member data export and the import wizard. See Turn on import.
  • Choose any optional import settings, such as the import prompt, the organization allowlist, and rollout by group.
  • Confirm that devices can reach the hosts that sign-in import needs.
  • Have the Primary Owner run an organization export for your records. The download link expires after 24 hours and may work only once, so download the file right away.
  • Send each wave the Checklist for users, along with your cutoff date.
  • Send developers the Checklist for developers, so they pull down cloud sessions before the cutoff date.
  • Postpone any changes to the claude.ai SSO connection and SCIM directory until the last import, or schedule the switch between waves.
Phase 4: Run a pilot, then move in waves

Who’s involved: device management, your champions, and your Anthropic account team

  • With MDM or a bootstrap server, deploy the configuration first, then the app, so users open the app directly into Claude Desktop on 3P. With the console, save the configuration first, then have users install the app and sign in.
  • Check a device with Help > Troubleshooting > Generate Diagnostic Report. In the exported file, deployment-mode.txt shows whether the app is in third-party mode.
  • Pilot with a mix of roles. Where they apply, include a CLI developer, a user of each restricted model, and a user from each identity group.
  • Test the import, each connector, web search on each network users work from, the Primary Owner’s history, and what users see when a request is flagged. Also test resuming a CLI session, cost reporting by user, and how spend appears in your provider’s billing console.
  • Fix what the pilot finds and update your user guide. Then move each wave, with launch training and office hours.
  • For each wave, track how many users have installed the app, signed in, imported, and are still active in week two. The desktop_claude_ai_import event in your telemetry is logged for each claude.ai history import. Users can import more than once, so count distinct users. It’s an info-level event, so set otlpDesktopLogLevel to info to receive it.
Phase 5: Wind down Claude Enterprise

Who’s involved: Primary Owner, identity admins, and network admins

  • On the cutoff date, have users finish their work in claude.ai and run the import one last time. Do this before you block claude.ai on your network, because sign-in import needs it. If you use the console, don’t block claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, or the hcaptcha.com hosts. Limit claude.ai and api.anthropic.com to your organizations with Tenant Restrictions instead. With MDM or a bootstrap server, the app also reads its update feed from claude.ai and api.anthropic.com by default. Before you block them, set updateViaUpdatesHost to true and allow releases.claude.com, or turn off auto-update and distribute new versions yourself. In Code sessions, Web Fetch checks each domain with api.anthropic.com and refuses the fetch if it can’t, so also set skipWebFetchPreflight to true before you block that host. Keep admin access after the cutoff date, so you can run final exports and remove users.
  • Keep users in the new deployment. With MDM or a bootstrap server, set deploymentMode to 3p in the managed profile that sets your provider or bootstrap keys (Claude Desktop 4.16336.0 or later). Until every device has updated, also set disableDeploymentModeChooser to true in the profile and, with a bootstrap server, in its response. Don’t set either key on devices that use the console. With the console, turn on Require this organization in Claude Desktop so members of both organizations must switch. That setting doesn’t enforce sign-in. To enforce it, remove your Claude Enterprise organization’s ID from forceLoginOrgUUID after the last wave has moved, except for users who keep Claude Enterprise.
  • For CLI users, narrow allowedProviders to the new provider, except on computers where users stay signed in to claude.ai in Claude Desktop, and retire your server-managed settings.
  • Control personal accounts on your domain and network with Restrict organization creation and Tenant Restrictions. If you use the console, include the new organization’s ID in the allowed list.
  • Run a final organization export and audit log export. A removed user’s data is still included in the Primary Owner’s exports.
  • Some work may have to stay on Claude Enterprise, for example under an access program your cloud provider doesn’t support yet, or for users who need the mobile apps. If so, keep those seats and reduce the size of the organization instead of closing it.
  • Remove users. With SCIM, users you remove from your IdP app are removed automatically. With JIT, they stay in your member list until an admin removes them. A user you remove only in Claude is added again the next time they log in with SSO. If your Enterprise Admin Console organization shares the SCIM directory, check how removing users from the IdP app affects it first. Removed users lose access immediately, but removal doesn’t delete their account or data.
  • To clear stored data sooner, you can shorten your custom data retention period. Anything outside the new period is scheduled for permanent deletion as soon as you save, so finish your exports first. The minimum period is 30 days, and it doesn’t cover the memory of users you’ve already removed. Chats in projects follow the project retention period instead, and artifacts published with a public link aren’t deleted.
  • Before you close anything, confirm with your Anthropic account team which domain and SSO settings the new deployment still relies on. Then talk to them about ending the plan. To delete the organization, the Primary Owner sends a request to Support.

After the move, contact your cloud provider about the inference service, and contact us about the desktop app and your rollout.

Plan for restricted models and access programs

Some access is granted to your organization through a verification program and then turned on for each platform you use. If your organization relies on a program or a restricted model today, plan it as a separate step and allow lead time for it.

This guide is for admins of organizations on Claude Enterprise plans.

This article is part of Move from Claude Enterprise to Claude Desktop on a cloud provider, which defines the terms wave, overlap period, and cutoff date.

Custom roles and model access settings are set in your Claude Enterprise organization. In Claude Desktop on 3P, your own configuration decides which models the picker offers, so plan to set these up again.

Cyber Verification Program (CVP)

For eligibility, access tiers, data retention, and how to apply, see Cyber Verification Program. For the move, plan for these points:

  • Link each cloud account: In the Verification Portal, link your AWS account, Google Cloud project, or Azure subscription. The article gives the steps for each platform. You need an Anthropic account to use the portal, even if you only use a cloud provider.
  • Check availability: On Amazon Bedrock, availability is limited. Check the program article for who’s eligible. On Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, accept the Advanced AI Safety Addendum, then enable advanced AI capabilities and data sharing for each model and location you use. See Google’s enrollment steps.
  • Allow lead time: On cloud providers, access to the program’s restricted model follows approval by about five business days. A committed contract adds a form and a private offer in the cloud marketplace.
  • Credentials: The security requirements don’t permit long-lived cloud credentials (for Defense Access, see the article for when this applies), and each approved user must sign in as themselves. Check them before you decide how users authenticate to your provider.
  • If you’re already approved: Each Claude organization needs its own application. To add a cloud account, link it to the same Anthropic organization in the Verification Portal. You don’t need a new application. Also turn on your tier for the new account.

Other programs

Each program lists the platforms it supports. For example, the Life Sciences Verification Program is in beta and isn’t yet available on third-party platforms. Access under it stays on Enterprise plans, Team plans, and the API.

Restricted models

Some models are available only through limited access programs like these. Covered Models lists them, and each model’s page lists the platforms it’s available on.

Control who can use which models

Where

Control

Good to know

Claude Desktop on 3P

inferenceModels lists what the picker offers. In the console, a permission policy for a group can narrow the list but can’t add to it. With MDM, scope a separate profile to each group.

A user in several groups gets the list from the highest-ranked of their policies that sets one. The lists aren’t combined.

Claude Code CLI

Set availableModels in managed settings. Add enforceAvailableModels to cover the Default option.

On a cloud provider, it arrives by file or OS policy, or through a Claude apps gateway.

Your cloud provider

AWS: Deny bedrock:InvokeModel by IAM policy or service control policy to block a model from the start. For a model already in use, deny all Bedrock actions on that model’s ARN.

Google Cloud: See Control access to Model Garden models.

Azure: A model must be deployed before it can be called, and an Azure Policy can restrict deployments to approved models. That policy is checked at deployment time.

These controls apply at the provider, outside the app.

Important: Set hard limits at your provider. The Claude Desktop on 3P and Claude Code lists above set what users can pick in those apps. Sessions on a cloud provider authenticate against your provider, and its access policies govern them. Removing a user from the console doesn’t end their access to the provider.

Plan identity and sign-in

A Claude Desktop on 3P deployment has several separate sign-ins, and most can use a different identity system. List them before you schedule your move. If you’re also changing identity providers (IdPs), the order of the two projects matters, because by default claude.ai accepts one IdP at a time.

This guide is for admins of organizations on Claude Enterprise plans.

This article is part of Move from Claude Enterprise to Claude Desktop on a cloud provider, which defines the terms wave, overlap period, and cutoff date.

Sign-ins your users will see

Sign-in

Who sees it

What it uses

claude.ai (your Claude Enterprise organization)

Every user, until their last import. The import wizard opens claude.ai in the browser to sign in and authorize.

The SSO connection held by your parent organization.

Enterprise Admin Console

Only users whose app is managed from the console. With MDM, a local file, or a bootstrap server, users have no Anthropic account.

A Claude account under the user’s work email, through your SSO if you connect it. SSO is recommended but not required. The sign-in expires about once a month.

Your provider

Every user, unless you deploy a shared key, a credentials file, or a credential helper.

IAM Identity Center, Google or Workforce Identity, or Entra ID. It’s separate from the Claude sign-in, and the app never sends Claude credentials to your provider.

Bootstrap server

Only deployments that use one with per-user sign-in.

Your own IdP. It’s independent of the inference sign-in, except in device-code mode, where one sign-in covers both if the gateway and the bootstrap server share an origin.

Connectors

Each user, once per connector.

The IdP of the connector’s vendor. The app stores each connector token on the device, so users connect each one again in the new app.

Claude Code CLI

Developers.

The cloud provider’s own credential chain. See Move Claude Code CLI users.

Connect your IdP to your cloud provider

Each provider’s setup guide explains how to connect your IdP.

  • Amazon Bedrock: Make your IdP the identity source for IAM Identity Center. AWS allows only one identity source per organization in AWS Organizations. Before you change it, read AWS’s considerations for changing your identity source.
  • Google Cloud: Use Workforce Identity Federation with an OIDC provider in the pool. A pool can federate one or more IdPs.
  • Microsoft Foundry: Foundry uses Entra ID directly. If you have Conditional Access rules, see Sign in through the OS identity broker.
  • LLM gateway: Users sign in to your IdP, and your gateway checks each user’s token.

If you’re changing IdPs

  • By default, claude.ai takes one IdP. Each parent organization links to one IdP, and all verified domains must use it. The exception is a beta: parent organizations enrolled in centralized management can connect more than one IdP. A domain can’t get a second IdP while any organization uses JIT provisioning, or while Microsoft Login is turned on for that domain. Outside the beta, you can’t run the old and new IdPs side by side there.
  • Follow our steps for switching IdPs. See Switching to a different Identity Provider (IdP). Resetting the SSO connection signs out all users. They can sign in by email link until the new connection is live. For Entra ID, see Microsoft Entra ID SSO setup.
  • Make sure email addresses match exactly. Claude matches SSO logins to seats by email. A mismatch in the new IdP creates duplicate accounts, and a SCIM email change removes the old user and creates a new one. Fix mismatches before anyone imports.
  • Check whether your Enterprise Admin Console organization shares the connection. If it uses the existing SSO connection, SCIM directory, and verified domains, one IdP serves both. Before you reset SSO or close the older organization, ask your Anthropic account team how it affects the Enterprise Admin Console organization and the devices it manages.

We recommend this order:

  • Connect the new IdP to your cloud provider first, and pilot sign-in there. On AWS, if IAM Identity Center already uses the old IdP, this step replaces that organization’s one identity source. You can’t pilot the two side by side in the same AWS organization.
  • If the old IdP will stay in service long enough, leave the claude.ai SSO connection alone until the last wave has imported.
  • If the old IdP retires sooner, make the switch between waves. Don’t switch while a wave is importing. Compare the email attributes in both IdPs first.
  • Keep claude.ai sign-in and member data export working until the final import is done.

Settings for the overlap period

  • Sign-in screen: Users can choose claude.ai or your provider configuration. deploymentMode set to 3p hides the claude.ai option (Claude Desktop 4.16336.0 or later). Set it in a device profile that also sets your connection. For earlier versions, also set disableDeploymentModeChooser to true. You can’t set either key in the console. Don’t set them on a device the console manages, because they make the app stop using the console.
  • Organization lock: forceLoginOrgUUID limits standard sign-in on the device to your organization. It also accepts a list of organization IDs. With the console, include your Enterprise Admin Console organization’s ID as well as your Claude Enterprise organization’s, and update devices to 2.37337.0 or later first. Otherwise, the console’s settings don’t apply.
  • Network allowlist: Tenant Restrictions uses a header that lists allowed organization IDs. Make sure it includes every organization your users still sign in to.
  • Users in two organizations: A console user who also belongs to another organization is asked whether to switch, and each switch restarts the app. Turn on Require this organization in Claude Desktop so users can’t dismiss the prompt. If your Claude Enterprise organization blocks other accounts in Claude Desktop, first add the Enterprise Admin Console organization’s ID to its Allowed organizations list.
  • Claude Code CLI: List both providers in allowedProviders during the overlap period. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR gives each account its own configuration directory.

Purchase and manage seats on Enterprise plans

This article covers how to add seats, manage your seat allocation, and handle member access on Enterprise plans. For pricing and billing details, see How am I billed for my Enterprise plan?

Permissions note: Only Owners and Primary Owners can purchase seats and access Organization settings > Organization and access. Admins and above can reassign seat types for members in Organization settings > Members. To check your role, click your name or initials in the lower left corner—your role is listed next to your organization’s plan type.

For information on adding and removing members from your organization, see Manage members on Team and Enterprise plans.

Important: The main sections of this article describe the current Enterprise seat model, which applies to all new Enterprise plans.

  • If your organization was provisioned before the transition to the single Enterprise seat and you see Chat and Chat + Claude Code seat types in Organization settings > Members, refer to Information for Chat and Chat + Claude Code plans.
    • HIPAA-ready Enterprise organizations are an exception: they are provisioned with separate Chat and Chat + Claude Code seat types and are not eligible for the single Enterprise seat billing model.
  • If you see Standard and Premium seat types, refer to Information for seat-based Enterprise plans.
  • Chat-only seats and Standard/Premium seats are no longer available for new contracts—both legacy plan types are transitioning to the single Enterprise seat at their next renewal.

Your seat type

Usage-based Enterprise plans use a single seat type: the Enterprise seat, priced per user per month (billed annually). This seat includes access to Claude on web, desktop, and mobile, as well as Claude Code.

Enterprise plans require a minimum of 20 seats.

Who can use a seat

Each Enterprise seat is assigned to one named individual, and only that person may use it. This applies to every Enterprise seat type, including legacy Chat, Chat + Claude Code, Standard, and Premium seats. This means:

  • Only the assigned user may sign in to the account. Users can’t share login credentials or let others use their account.
  • Users can’t use another user’s account to get around their own spend limits or usage limits.

Reassigning a seat is meant for normal team changes, such as a user joining, leaving, or changing roles. It isn’t designed for rotating one seat among several active users. To give someone else access, assign them their own seat.

Purchase new seats

You can add seats to your Enterprise plan at any time during your annual term. New seats are prorated for the remainder of your billing cycle and charged immediately.

  • Log in with your Owner or Primary Owner account.
  • Go to Organization settings > Organization and access.
  • Click “Manage” under Total seats.
  • Click “Add or change seats.”
  • Enter the number of seats you’d like to add.
  • Review your changes and the prorated charge before confirming.
  • Click “Confirm & purchase” to finalize.

Note: You can also purchase a seat while adding a new member. If you don’t have an available seat when inviting someone, you’ll be prompted to purchase one.

For details on how seat additions are billed, see How am I billed for my Enterprise plan?

Remove seats

Self-serve Enterprise plans: Seats cannot be removed during your annual term. You can add seats at any time, but reductions to your seat count only take effect at renewal. If you need to make an exception, contact our Sales team to discuss converting to a sales-assisted plan.

Sales-assisted Enterprise plans: Contact your account manager to discuss changes to your seat allocation.

Removing a member from your organization is different from reducing your seat count. When you remove a member, their seat becomes available to assign to someone else, so your total seat allocation and bill don’t change. To reduce your bill, you’ll need to reduce your total seat allocation. See Manage members on Team and Enterprise plans for instructions on removing members.

Temporarily remove a member’s access

The No seat assigned option lets you temporarily remove a member’s access to Claude without removing them from your organization. This is useful for contractors or team members who need intermittent access.

To unassign a member:

  • Go to Organization settings > Members.
  • Find the member you want to unassign.
  • Click the dropdown under Tier.
  • Select “No seat assigned.”

To restore their access, repeat the process and select “Enterprise seat.”

Note: Members with no seat assigned remain part of your organization but can’t use Claude until you reassign them a seat. They do not count toward your organization’s seat limit. Pending invitations do count. If “Add member” is unavailable even though seats show as available, revoke pending invitations that won’t be accepted, or purchase additional seats.

Seat assignment with JIT or SCIM provisioning

Users provisioned via JIT or SCIM are automatically assigned an Enterprise seat when they’re added, provided one is available in your allocation. If no seat is available, provisioning will not complete until an owner purchases an additional seat.

Admins and above can manually adjust a member’s status (e.g., remove their seat assignment) afterward in Organization settings > Members.

Cancel your Enterprise plan

Self-serve Enterprise plans: An Owner or Primary Owner can cancel your plan from Organization settings > Billing. Cancellation takes effect at the end of your current annual billing cycle—your organization will continue to have access until then.

Sales-assisted Enterprise plans: Reach out to your Anthropic Contact or our Sales team to discuss cancellation.

Information for Chat and Chat + Claude Code plans

Important: Chat and Chat + Claude Code are legacy seat types that are no longer available for new Enterprise contracts. This section only applies to organizations that were provisioned with these seat types before the transition to the single Enterprise seat. If you recently signed a new Enterprise contract, the main sections of this article apply to you—your plan uses the single Enterprise seat, which includes Claude Code access for all members.

Some existing usage-based Enterprise organizations currently have two seat types: Chat and Chat + Claude Code. If you see these seat types in Organization settings > Members, this section applies to you. Your plan will transition to the single Enterprise seat model at your next contract renewal—see below for more information.

Seat types

Seat type

What’s included

Chat

Claude on web, desktop, and mobile apps

Chat + Claude Code

Everything in Chat, plus Claude Code access

You can mix and match seat types based on your team’s needs. Assign Chat + Claude Code seats to team members who need coding workflows, while keeping others on Chat seats.

Reassign users between seat types

You can move users between Chat and Chat + Claude Code seats within your existing allocation.

  • Go to Organization settings > Members.
  • Find the member you want to reassign.
  • Click the dropdown under Tier.
  • Select “Chat” or “Chat + Claude Code.”

Members moved from Chat + Claude Code to Chat will lose Claude Code access, and vice versa.

The Tier dropdown only shows seat types your plan already owns. If your plan includes Chat + Claude Code seats but they’re all assigned, you’ll be prompted to purchase one. If your plan has no seats of that type, see Purchase new seats above to add one first.

Swap users between seat types

If all your Chat + Claude Code seats are assigned and you need to move one user to that type while moving another off it, use No seat assigned to free up a seat first.

Example: You have ten Chat + Claude Code seats, all assigned. You want to move User A (currently on Chat + Claude Code) to Chat, and move User B (currently on Chat) to Chat + Claude Code — without purchasing an additional seat.

  • Go to Organization settings > Members.
  • Find User A and change their seat type to “No seat assigned.” This frees up one Chat + Claude Code seat.
  • Find User B and change their seat type to “Chat + Claude Code.” They now occupy the freed seat.
  • Find User A and change their seat type to “Chat.”
Seat assignment with JIT or SCIM provisioning

Users provisioned via JIT or SCIM are automatically assigned to the highest-available seat type (Chat + Claude Code, if available) when they’re added. Admins and above can manually reassign seat types afterward in Organization settings > Members.

You can also use Advanced Group Mappings with JIT or SCIM to provision users directly to a specific seat type.

Transition to the single Enterprise seat

Note: HIPAA-ready organizations are provisioned with separate Chat and Chat + Claude Code seat types and are not eligible for the unified seat type.

At your next renewal, you will switch to the single Enterprise seat model upon signing a new contract. This seat includes Claude Code, Cowork, Chat and more.

Reach out to your Anthropic Contact or our Sales team with questions about your upcoming renewal.

Information for seat-based Enterprise plans

Important: Standard and Premium are legacy seat types that are no longer available for new Enterprise contracts. This section only applies to organizations that were provisioned with these seat types before the transition to usage-based billing. If you recently signed a new Enterprise contract, the main sections of this article apply to you.

Some Enterprise organizations are on older seat-based plans with a different billing structure than the usage-based model described above. If you see Standard and Premium seats in Organization settings > Members, this section applies to you.

Seat types

Seat type

What’s included

Standard

Core Enterprise features and usage limits

Premium

Everything in Standard, plus higher usage limits

Note: Only Admins and above can see each user’s seat type, shown in the Tier column in Organization settings > Members. Other users can’t see their own seat type anywhere in Claude. If you need to confirm whether your seat is Standard or Premium, ask an Owner or Admin in your organization.

Reassign users between seat types

You can move users between Standard and Premium seats within your existing allocation.

  • Go to Organization settings > Members.
  • Find the member you want to reassign.
  • Click the dropdown under Tier.
  • Select “Standard” or “Premium.”

Members moved from Premium to Standard will have lower usage limits, and vice versa.

The Tier dropdown only shows seat types your plan already owns. If your plan includes Premium seats but they’re all assigned, reassigning another user to Premium will prompt you to purchase an additional seat. If your plan has no seats of that type, see Purchase new seats above to add one first.

Swap users between seat types

If all your Premium seats are assigned and you need to move one user to Premium while moving another to Standard, use No seat assigned to free up a seat first.

Example: You have ten Premium seats, all assigned. You want to move User A (currently on Premium) to Standard, and move User B (currently on Standard) to Premium—without purchasing an additional seat.

  • Go to Organization settings > Members.
  • Find User A and change their seat type to “No seat assigned.” This frees up one Premium seat.
  • Find User B and change their seat type to “Premium.” They now occupy the freed seat.
  • Find User A and change their seat type to “Standard.”
Billing and usage credits

Seat-based Enterprise plans charge a flat monthly fee per seat that includes usage limits. Owners can enable usage credits to allow team members to continue working after reaching their seat’s usage limits. For details, see Manage usage credits for Team and seat-based Enterprise plans.

For specific information about seat-based Enterprise pricing, reach out to your Anthropic Contact or our Sales team.

Transition to the single Enterprise seat

At your next contract renewal, your plan will transition to the usage-based single Enterprise seat model described in the main sections of this article. If you’d like to migrate before your renewal, reach out to your Anthropic Contact or our Sales team.

Purchase and manage seats on Team plans

Seat management allows Team plan owners to control their organization’s seat allocation, assign users to different seat types, and manage billing. For pricing and billing details, see How is my Team plan bill calculated?

Permissions note: Only Owners and Primary Owners can purchase seats and access Organization settings > Billing. Admins and above can reassign seat types for members in Organization settings > Members.

For information on adding and removing members from your organization, see Manage members on Team and Enterprise plans.

Understanding seat types

Team plans offer two seat types:

Seat type

What’s included

Standard

Base features, usage limits, and Claude Code access

Premium

Everything in Standard, plus higher usage limits

Organizations can mix and match seat types based on team needs. Assign Premium seats to power users who need more capacity, while keeping other team members on Standard seats.

Your plan has a total seat allocation (e.g., 30 Standard seats and 10 Premium seats). Within that allocation, you can assign and reassign users to different seat types as needed.

Note: Only Admins and above can see each user’s seat type, shown in the Tier column in Organization settings > Members. Other users can’t see their own seat type anywhere in Claude. If you need to confirm whether your seat is Standard or Premium, ask an Owner or Admin in your organization.

Who can use a seat

Each seat on a Team plan is assigned to one named individual, and only that person may use it. This means:

  • Only the assigned user may sign in to the account. Users can’t share login credentials or let others use their account.
  • Users can’t route their work through another user’s account to use that user’s remaining usage.
  • Unused usage on one seat can’t be transferred to another user.

If a user regularly needs more capacity, an owner can move them to a Premium seat or turn on usage credits. Learn more about managing usage credits for Team and seat-based Enterprise plans.

Reassigning a seat is meant for normal team changes, such as a user joining, leaving, or changing roles. It isn’t designed for rotating one seat among several active users.

Purchase new seats

Important: If you want to upgrade an existing member from Standard to Premium and already have Premium seats available, you don’t need to purchase a new seat. Use the seat tier reassignment in Organization settings > Members instead. See Upgrade a Standard seat to Premium below.

Follow these steps to add seats to your plan’s total allocation:

  • Log in with your Owner or Primary Owner account.
  • Navigate to Organization settings > Organization and access.
  • Click “Manage” under “Total seats.”
  • In the “Seat breakdown” modal, click “Add or change seats.”
  • Click the “+” next to the seat type you want to add (Standard or Premium).
  • Click “Next” to review your purchase details and confirm the billing impact.
  • Check the confirmation box before continuing.
  • Click “Confirm & purchase” to complete the transaction.

Note: You can also purchase seats while adding a new member. The seat type selector only shows seat types your plan already owns—if all seats of the selected type are assigned, you’ll be prompted to purchase one.

Reduce your seat allocation

You can reduce the total number of seats on your Team plan:

  • Log in with your Owner or Primary Owner account.
  • Navigate to Organization settings > Organization and access.
  • If needed, remove members or reassign them to free up the seats you want to eliminate.
  • Click “Manage” under Total seats.
  • Click “Add or change seats” in the Seat breakdown modal.
  • Click the “-” next to the seat type you want to reduce.
  • Click “Next” to review the changes.
  • Check the confirmation box and click “Confirm & purchase” to complete the change.

Reducing your organization’s seat count takes effect at your next renewal (on the annual renewal date for annual plans). There is no prorated refund at the time you submit this change.

Assign and reassign seat types

You can move users between Standard and Premium seats within your existing allocation.

To reassign a user’s seat type:

  • Go to Organization settings > Members.
  • Find the member you want to reassign.
  • Click the dropdown under Tier.
  • Select “Standard” or “Premium.”

Members moved from Premium to Standard will have lower usage limits, and vice versa.

To move several members from Premium to Standard, do not use the per-member Tier dropdown. Instead, open Organization and access, click “Manage” under Total seats, then “Add or change seats,” and set the Premium and Standard totals in one submission. You can set Premium below the number of members currently assigned to it: those members are moved onto Standard seats automatically at renewal. The Standard total cannot be lower than your current billable members.

Only one scheduled seat change can be pending at a time. Submitting a new one, adding seats, or accepting a new invite replaces the pending change.

Moving a member from Premium to Standard takes effect at your next renewal (on the annual renewal date for annual plans). There is no prorated refund at the time you submit this change.

Upgrade a Standard seat to Premium

Upgrading a member from Standard to Premium is a reassignment, not a new purchase. You don’t need to buy an additional seat unless your Premium allocation is already full.

Note: The Tier dropdown only shows seat types your plan already owns. If your plan has zero Premium seats, Premium won’t appear as an option yet. First add at least one Premium seat by following the steps in Purchase new seats above. Once your plan includes a Premium seat, you can select “Premium” from the dropdown.

  1. Go to Organization settings > Members.

  2. Find the member assigned to a Standard seat you want to upgrade.

  3. Click the dropdown under Tier.

  4. Select “Premium.”

If your plan includes Premium seats but they’re all assigned, you’ll be prompted to purchase an additional one at this point. The upgrade is prorated based on your billing cycle, and you’ll be charged the price difference immediately.

What if I don’t have an available seat?

If your plan includes Premium seats but they’re all assigned, reassigning another user to Premium will prompt you to purchase an additional Premium seat. If your plan has no Premium seats at all, see Purchase new seats above to add one first.

Swap users between seat types

Selecting No seat assigned lets you temporarily remove a user from a seat without removing them from your organization. This is useful when you need to swap people between seat types within your existing allocation.

Example: You have five Premium seats, all assigned. You want to move User A (currently on Premium) to Standard, and move User B (currently on Standard) to Premium—without purchasing an additional seat.

  • Go to Organization settings > Members.
  • Find User A and change their seat tier to “No seat assigned.” This frees up one Premium seat.
  • Find User B and change their seat tier to “Premium.” They now occupy the available Premium seat.
  • Find User A and change their seat tier to “Standard.”

Note: Members with no seat assigned remain part of your organization but can’t use Claude until you reassign them a seat. They do not count toward your organization’s seat limit. Pending invitations do count. If “Add member” is unavailable even though seats show as available, revoke pending invitations that won’t be accepted, or purchase additional seats.

Seat assignment with JIT or SCIM provisioning

Users provisioned via JIT or SCIM are automatically assigned to the highest-available seat type when they’re added. Admins and above can manually reassign seat types afterward in Organization settings > Members.

You can also enable group mappings with JIT or SCIM to provision users directly to a specific seat type.

Understanding billing

  • New seats are prorated based on your billing cycle and charged immediately.
  • Seat type upgrades (Standard → Premium) are prorated and charged immediately for the price difference.
  • Removing members does not trigger an immediate credit or refund. The seat becomes available to assign to another member. To reduce your bill, you’ll need to reduce your plan’s total seat allocation.

For detailed billing calculations and examples, see How is my Team plan bill calculated?

Restrict verified-domain connectors to your Enterprise

This article explains how to prevent Claude accounts outside your Enterprise organization from connecting certain services, like Gmail and Slack, using an email address on your verified domains. Use the Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise setting to keep company data from reaching personal Claude accounts through connectors.

This setting is available to Owners, Primary Owners, and custom roles with the Identity & Access permission set to Manage on the Enterprise plan. Your Enterprise organization needs at least one verified domain.

How it works

When you turn on Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise, only Claude accounts in your Enterprise organization can connect the supported connectors using an email address on your verified domains. Anyone who tries to make one of these connections from a Claude account outside your Enterprise is blocked. This setting applies to your entire Enterprise. You manage it at the parent organization level, and it applies to all child organizations.

This check relies on the connected service sharing the account’s identity during the connection process. For supported connectors, Claude can confirm the email domain of the account being connected and enforce the restriction. When a service doesn’t share account identity, Claude can’t perform the check and the connection proceeds normally.

This setting applies to the following connectors:

  • Airtable
  • Asana
  • Atlassian
  • Box
  • Canva
  • Figma
  • Gmail
  • Google Calendar
  • Google Docs
  • Google Drive
  • Google Sheets
  • Google Slides
  • HubSpot
  • Linear
  • Microsoft 365
  • Miro
  • Notion
  • Slack
  • Smartsheet
  • Tableau

You can also view the current list in Organization settings > Organization and access. Contact our support team to request additional connectors.

For example, someone has two Claude accounts: a personal account using their personal email, and a work account using their work email. The work email is on a domain your Enterprise organization has verified.

When the setting is off, they can sign in to Claude with their personal account and connect the Gmail account they use for work. That moves company information outside your organization’s controls.

When the setting is on, they can’t connect their work Gmail from their personal account. They can still connect it from their work account. That keeps company information inside your organization’s controls.

Prerequisites

Before you can turn on this setting, your Enterprise organization must verify your domain.

Turn on the restriction

  • Navigate to Organization settings > Organization and access.
  • Scroll to Connector domain restriction.
  • Toggle on “Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise.”

You can turn off this setting at any time. It’s separate from domain capture, which can’t be reversed once enabled.

What people see when a connection is restricted

If someone tries to make a connection that’s restricted, the connection fails at sign-in with this message:

“This corporate identity belongs to an Enterprise that manages access through their own Claude account. Sign in to your organization’s Claude account to use this connection.”

What the setting doesn’t do

  • It doesn’t restrict connections in the other direction. When the setting is on, people in your Enterprise can still connect services for personal use to their Enterprise Claude account. For example, they can connect their personal Gmail account.
  • It doesn’t replace data loss prevention. It’s a safeguard against accidentally connecting a work account to the wrong Claude account, not a control against deliberate data movement.
  • It doesn’t disconnect existing connections. The restriction applies only to new connection attempts. Connections made before you turned on the setting stay connected.
  • It doesn’t notify admins. Only the person attempting the connection sees the message if it fails.

Frequently asked questions

How is this different from domain claiming?

Domain claiming closes existing personal Claude accounts on your domain and lets each person bring what they can into your Enterprise workspace. This setting leaves Claude accounts where they are, and makes it so that only Claude accounts in your Enterprise organization can connect supported connectors using an email address on your verified domains. Learn more about claiming and migrating accounts on your domain.

What should someone do if their connection is blocked?

Sign in to your organization’s Claude account and make the connection there. Anyone who doesn’t have a Claude account in your organization should contact their admin for access.

Are all connections on a supported connector covered?

Coverage depends on the identity information each service provides. In a small number of cases (for example, some Canva Education (.edu) accounts) the service does not share the identity details needed to apply the restriction, and those connections are allowed as normal. Where the restriction can’t be evaluated, the connection is allowed rather than blocked.

Roles and permissions

What an individual can see and do in their Team or Enterprise plan account is dictated by their role. Roles are provisioned with the following permissions.

Important notes about the Primary Owner role:

  • Team and Enterprise organizations can only have one Primary Owner.
  • The Primary Owner seat uses one of your plan’s licenses.
  • Your organization’s Primary Owner can be a service account that isn’t tied to an individual user.
  • If you’re unsure of your organization’s Primary Owner, you can check by going to Settings > Account.

About custom roles (Enterprise plans only): Enterprise plans support custom roles, which let you control feature access at the group level. Members with roles set to “Custom” have no default permissions—their access is determined entirely by the custom roles assigned to their groups. Because these members have no built-in permissions, they don’t appear in the tables below.

To learn more, refer to the following articles:
