Set a default model for your organization

This guide explains how to choose the Claude model that new conversations start on across your organization. You can set one default for your whole organization, or set different defaults for specific custom roles. You can also make every new conversation start on your default model and effort level, even after users pick a different model.

Default model settings are available for Enterprise plan organizations. Primary Owners, Owners, and members whose custom role grants the Identity & Access permission can manage them in Organization settings > Models.

You can also set the default effort level that new conversations start on, or leave it on Anthropic’s recommended default effort. To control which models members can use and cap the effort level they can select, see Manage model access for your organization.

How default models work

When you set or change a default model, it replaces the model currently selected in each member’s model picker. New conversations in chat, Cowork, Claude Code, Claude for Office, Claude Design, and Claude Science then start on the model you’ve chosen.

Note: Not all models are available in every product. If the selected model is not available in the product, Anthropic’s recommendation is used as default.

Users can still select a different model for any conversation. By default, Claude remembers each user’s last selection, so their next conversation starts on whichever model they last used. When you update the default again, the new default replaces their selection. To have every new conversation start on the default instead, see Always start new chats on the default model below.

For example: you set the organization default to Claude Sonnet 4.6, and every member’s new conversations start on Sonnet 4.6. A member switches a conversation to Claude Opus 4.7, so their next conversations start on Opus 4.7. When you later change the organization default, the new default replaces their selection again. If you turn on Always start with the default model and effort level, their next chat starts on Sonnet 4.6 no matter which model they used last.

You can set a default at two levels:

  • Organization default: applies to every member of your organization.
  • Custom role default: applies to members assigned to that role and takes precedence over the organization default.

Alongside the default model, you can set a default effort level. New conversations on the default model start at that effort level. Members can still change the effort level for any conversation, within the organization’s effort cap for that model and any cap set by their custom role. If the default effort is higher than a cap that applies to a member, their conversations start at the highest level they’re allowed.

Note: Members on Claude Code CLI versions earlier than 2.1.199 won’t pick up the organization default. Versions 2.1.196 through 2.1.198 also had a bug where setting a specific organization default caused other enabled models to disappear from the model picker in the CLI and VS Code extension; updating to 2.1.199 or later resolves both.

For member-facing CLI instructions, see Claude Code model configuration.

For member-facing instructions on switching models, see Change the model, effort, and thinking settings.

Set the organization default model

The organization default applies to every member. To set it:

  • Navigate to Organization settings > Models.
  • Under Default model, select an option under the model dropdown list:
    • “Use Anthropic’s recommended default”: Anthropic’s recommended model that updates automatically when new models are released.
    • “Choose a specific model”: a specific model that won’t change when new models are released.
  • If you select “Choose a specific model,” choose a model from the list. Only models enabled under Model access on the same page can be selected.
  • Click “Save changes.”

Set the default effort level

The default effort level applies to new conversations on the organization default model. To set it:

  • Navigate to Organization settings > Models.
  • Under Default model, select an option under the effort level dropdown list:
    • “Use Anthropic’s recommended default effort”: Anthropic’s recommended effort level for the default model, which updates automatically when recommendations change.
    • Choose a level from the list. Available effort levels differ depending on the model, and some models don’t support effort level settings at all.
  • Click “Save changes.”

The default effort level can’t be higher than the organization’s effort cap for the default model. If you lower that cap below the current default effort, the default effort is lowered to match.

Always start new chats on the default model

By default, each user’s next conversation starts on the model they last used. Turn on this setting to have every new conversation start on your organization’s default model and default effort level instead.

  • Navigate to Organization settings > Models.
  • Turn on Always start with the default model and effort level.
  • Click “Save.”

With this setting on:

  • Every new conversation starts on the default model at the default effort level.
  • Users can still change the model and effort level within a conversation. Their next conversation starts on the default again.
  • When the default model changes, new conversations move to the new default. For example, if you use Anthropic’s recommended default and the recommendation moves to a newer model, every user’s next conversation starts on the newer model.

This setting applies in chat, Cowork, Claude Code, Claude for Office, Claude Design, and Claude Science.

In projects

Projects keep their own model selection. Claude remembers the model each user last picked in each project, and this setting doesn’t override that choice in existing chat projects. With Always start with the default model and effort level turned on:

  • New projects start on the default model.
  • Existing chat projects start on the model the user last selected in that project.
  • New Cowork tasks in a project start on the default model.
For a custom role

Custom roles that set their own default model have the same switch in the role editor.

  • Navigate to Organization settings > Roles.
  • Click the role you want to edit.
  • Select the “Models” tab and choose a default model for the role.
  • Turn on Always start with the default model and effort level.
  • Click “Save role.”

Set a default model for a custom role

Custom role defaults let you set different starting models for different teams. For example, you can keep most of your organization on the recommended default while a specific group starts on a different model.

  • Navigate to Organization settings > Roles.
  • Click the role you want to edit, or create a new role.
  • Select the Models tab, then under Default model, select a model. Roles are set to “Organization default” unless you choose a specific model. Only models the role has access to can be selected.
  • Click “Save role” to save your changes.

A role’s default model takes precedence over the organization default for members assigned to that role.

If a member belongs to multiple groups whose custom roles set different default models, the most capable model will be the default. Capability is determined first by model family (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus), then release date, so more capable model families take precedence, and newer models within the same family take precedence.

The role’s effort cap for the default model, if any, still applies. A role can’t set an effort cap higher than the organization’s cap for that model. For details, see Limit the maximum effort level for a custom role.

Note: Custom roles only affect members whose role is set to “Custom.” Members with the User, Admin, or Owner roles get the default model from the organization setting, not from custom roles.

For details on creating roles and assigning them to groups, see Manage custom roles on Enterprise plans.

Set the default effort level for a custom role

The default effort level applies to new conversations on the role’s default model. To set it:

  • Navigate to Organization settings > Roles.
  • Click the role you want to edit, or create a new role.
  • Select the Models tab, then under Default model, select a model. Roles are set to “Organization default” unless you choose a specific model. Only models the role has access to can be selected.
  • Under Default model, select an option under the effort level dropdown list:
    • Use Anthropic’s recommended default effort: Anthropic’s recommended effort level for the default model, which updates automatically when recommendations change.
    • Choose a level from the list. Available effort levels differ depending on the model, and some models don’t support effort level settings at all.
  • Click “Save changes.”

The default effort level can’t be higher than the organization’s effort cap for the default model. If you lower that cap below the current default effort, the default effort is lowered to match.

Default model and Claude Code managed settings

If your organization also configures Claude Code through managed-settings.json, the model setting there takes precedence. When model is set in managed settings, Claude Code CLI and IDE start on that model and ignore the default you set in Organization settings > Models.

If managed-settings.json specifies availableModels that doesn’t contain the default model, Claude CLI bypasses availableModels and starts on the selected default model unless enforceAvailableModels is set.

Managed settings for models apply only to local Claude Code sessions in your terminal or IDE, not to cloud sessions or to Claude Code in Claude Desktop. For consistent behavior across all Claude Code surfaces, we recommend setting the default here alone. For more on managed settings, see Claude Code settings.

Set organization instructions

Organization instructions let owners of Team and Enterprise plans set custom instructions that Claude follows in every conversation across your organization. Use them to apply communication standards, formatting requirements, compliance guidance, or domain-specific context that should show up everywhere your team works with Claude.

Organization instructions are available to Owners and Primary Owners on Team and Enterprise plans.

How organization and user instructions interact

Claude supports two levels of instructions. Understanding how they interact helps owners and the people on your team get the most out of both.

Level

Set by

Scope

Visibility

Organization instructions

Owners and Primary Owners

All people in your organization, every conversation

Only Owners and above can view or edit

Individual user instructions

Each user

That individual’s conversations only

Only that user can view or edit

When both are set, organization instructions take precedence. If an individual instruction directly contradicts an organization instruction, Claude favors the organization-level instruction. For example, if an organization instruction says “Always respond in formal English” but an individual instruction says “use a casual tone,” Claude responds formally.

Individual instructions still apply for anything the organization instructions don’t address.

Note: Instruction prioritization relies on prompt-level instructions. In rare edge cases involving directly contradictory instructions, behavior may vary. Test your instructions to confirm they produce the results you expect.

Set up organization instructions

You need at least an Owner role to configure organization instructions.

  • Go to Organization settings > Organization and access.
  • Find the Organization instructions section.
  • Enter your instructions in the text area. The maximum length is 3,000 characters.
  • Click “Save changes.”
  • Changes may take up to an hour to take effect across Claude products.

To remove instructions entirely, clear the text area and click “Save changes.”

Best practices

Keep instructions concise and clear. Organization instructions are included in every message sent by everyone in your organization, so shorter instructions help keep conversations efficient. Aim for direct, specific guidance rather than lengthy explanations.

Be specific about what you want. Instead of vague instructions like “be professional,” give concrete direction such as “Respond in formal English. Don’t use contractions, slang, or emojis.”

Focus on consistent behaviors. Organization instructions work best for instructions that should apply uniformly across every conversation—response formatting standards, tone requirements, or organization-wide context.

Avoid conflicting instructions. If your organization instructions contradict each other, Claude may not follow either one reliably. Review your instructions as a whole to make sure they’re consistent.

Don’t try to override safety behaviors. Organization preferences can’t disable Claude’s built-in safety guidelines or content policies. Instructions that conflict with Claude’s core training won’t be followed.

Test your instructions. After saving, start a new conversation to verify Claude is following your instructions. Try a few different types of questions to confirm the instructions work across a range of topics.

Review and update regularly. As your organization’s needs change, revisit your instructions to make sure they’re still relevant. Removing outdated instructions keeps Claude’s responses focused.

Example instructions

Team identity. “Address the team as the Acme Platform team. When users ask about ‘our product,’ they mean Acme Cloud.”

Communication standards. “Respond in formal English. Use active voice. Avoid contractions and emojis.”

Response formatting. “Prefer concise responses under 300 words. Use bullet points for lists with three or more items.”

Domain context. “Our team works in healthcare claims processing. When users mention ‘claims,’ they’re referring to insurance claims, not legal claims.”

Referral guidance. “When users ask about HR policies, direct them to [email protected] rather than giving specific policy advice.”

Data handling reminders. “Don’t include customer names, account numbers, or other personally identifiable information in responses or generated artifacts.”

Set up and manage the new unified Claude experience for your Enterprise organization

The new unified Claude experience brings chat and Cowork together on web, desktop, and mobile. Members no longer choose between chat and Cowork before they start. Every conversation starts as a chat, and when a task needs to run code or work with files, Claude continues the same conversation in an isolated cloud sandbox managed by Anthropic, then returns the finished work for review.

This article explains how admins turn on the new unified Claude experience, which settings apply to it, and how it fits your security, compliance, and data retention setup.

The new unified Claude experience is available on Enterprise plans, where it appears in admin settings as Chat and Cowork unified. It’s off by default in existing organizations and turns on by default on November 16, 2026.

How the new unified Claude experience works

  • One conversation, two modes. The new unified Claude experience starts as a chat and moves into a Cowork cloud session when a task needs agentic work. Members aren’t asked to switch modes.
  • Longer tasks run in an isolated cloud environment. Each conversation that needs one gets its own virtual machine, managed by Anthropic. After a few minutes idle, the virtual machine is stopped and its disk is saved as an encrypted snapshot. The sandbox environment expires 30 days after it was created.
  • The conversation stays on record. Chat history, sharing, export, the Compliance API, and your data retention setting all work from the conversation.
  • Work moves across devices. Members can start a task on the desktop app and pick it up on web or mobile.
  • Local access stays optional. Through the Claude desktop app, members can link their computers so Claude can work with local folders, local MCP servers, and applications. Your Computer access and device policies govern this.

Before you begin

The new unified Claude experience requires two capabilities to be on for your organization:

  • Chat, since chat is where every conversation starts.
  • Cloud code execution and file creation, since agentic work runs remotely.

It doesn’t require Cowork or Cowork in the cloud to be on. It is meant to replace both over time.

If members have earlier Cowork tasks that ran on their computers, keep Cowork on for their roles and your organization while they still need those tasks. These tasks don’t need Cowork in the cloud. When Cowork is off for a member’s role or your organization, those tasks open read-only, and scheduled tasks on that member’s computer stop. Before you turn Cowork off, ask members to type /export in each task they want to keep. This saves the task’s transcript as a zip file for reference only. It can’t be reopened as a task.

Earlier cloud tasks don’t need Cowork or Cowork in the cloud. They keep working with Chat and Cowork unified as long as the role has Chat and Code execution and file creation, plus Scheduled tasks for scheduled ones.

Your organization today

What to do

Chat only

Turn on Chat and Cowork unified. You don’t need to turn on Cowork or Cowork in the cloud separately. Make sure Cloud code execution and file creation is on.

Cowork only, or Cowork and Cowork in the cloud

Turn on the Chat capability, then turn on Chat and Cowork unified. Make sure Cloud code execution and file creation is on.

Chat and Cowork

Make sure Cloud code execution and file creation is on, then turn on Chat and Cowork unified.

The new unified Claude experience isn’t available yet for organizations that use zero data retention (ZDR), the HIPAA-ready configuration, or customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK). See Current limitations below.

Turn on the new unified Claude experience

For your whole organization
  • Sign in to Claude as an Owner or Primary Owner.
  • Go to Organization settings > Capabilities.
  • Turn on Chat and Cowork unified.
  • If you have eligible custom roles (roles with both Chat and code execution selected), a list opens with every eligible role selected, including roles where you turned it off. Roles without Chat or code execution are grayed out and not selected. Clear any role that shouldn’t have it, then confirm.
  • Ask members to refresh the Claude app if they don’t see the new experience right away.

This turns on the new unified Claude experience for members with the User, Admin, Owner or Primary Owner role. Members on a custom role get it only if their role also includes Chat and Cowork unified.

Scheduled tasks and session history will continue working after the change. You don’t need to update or recreate anything. Turning off Cowork for a role or your organization is a separate change that affects tasks on members’ computers. See Before you begin above.

If you haven’t changed this setting

On November 16, 2026, Chat and Cowork unified turns on by default if no admin has turned it on or off for your organization. Owners and Primary Owners can turn it off at any time in Organization settings > Capabilities. If the setting was already turned on or off, that choice stays.

If Chat or Cloud code execution and file creation is off, nothing turns on. After November 16, the new experience turns on as soon as both are on.

Custom roles on December 8, 2026: If your organization is still on by default, the new unified Claude experience turns on for custom roles that have both Chat and code execution selected, even if an admin turned it off for that role. Admins can turn it off again by role after that. If an admin has turned it on or off for your organization, this change doesn’t apply.

For specific members, using roles

The organization setting above must also be on. Once it is, everyone with the User, Admin, Owner or Primary Owner role has access. Before you turn it on, move anyone who shouldn’t have it to a custom role with Chat and Cowork unified turned off. New roles start with All capabilities, which includes it.

When you turn it on for your organization, clear that role in the list that opens, because every eligible role starts selected. If your organization is still on by default instead, it turns on for eligible roles on December 8, 2026, even if you turned it off for them.

If your organization uses custom roles, you can grant the new unified Claude experience to specific roles:

  • Go to Organization settings > Roles.
  • Open the role you want to update and go to “Capabilities.”
  • Turn on Chat and Cowork unified for that role.
  • Assign the role to the members who should have access. You can sync role membership through SCIM to add members in waves.

Access is checked on every request. If you remove a member’s role or turn the setting off, they lose access to the new unified Claude experience.

To learn how to create a role, see Set up role-based permissions on Enterprise plans.

Recommended rollout
  • Share this article with your IT, security, and procurement teams.
  • Complete your security review. Most teams review two components they already know: Claude chat and Cowork in the cloud. If a review of Cowork in the cloud is already underway, it carries over.
  • Start in your sandbox organization, if you have one, or with a pilot group through a role. If you pilot through a role, clear every other role you can in the list when you turn on the organization setting. Built-in roles and roles on “All capabilities” or “All generally available” can’t be cleared, so users with those roles get it too unless you move them first.
  • Review your network egress, connector, sharing, and Computer access settings before you turn the experience on.
  • Monitor usage and gather feedback for two to four weeks, then expand in waves.

Admin settings that apply to the new unified Claude experience

Setting

Where

How it applies to the new unified Claude experience

Turns the new unified Claude experience on for the organization. Changes are recorded in the activity feed.

Chat and Cowork unified (per role)

Organization settings > Roles > Capabilities

Grants the new unified Claude experience to members of a role.

Allow network egress

Organization settings > Capabilities > Code execution

Controls which internet destinations code in the sandbox can reach: off, package managers only, a custom list of domains, or all domains. Off by default for Enterprise.

Connector policies (Blocked, Needs approval, per-role restrictions)

Organization settings

Enforced by Anthropic outside the sandbox, on every connector call.

Organization settings

When off, members can’t give a connector tool a standing approval, and Claude asks each time.

Organization settings

When off, users can’t let Claude act without asking for approval — including using tools, editing files, and browsing websites. This specifically applies to scheduled tasks and the built-in browser in the unified experience.

Admin API

Organization settings

Open Telemetry (OTEL)

Organization settings

Device policy for the Claude desktop app

Your device management (MDM) tool

On managed computers, limits which folders can be connected, disables user-added local MCP servers and extensions, can require sign-in to your organization, and can turn off computer use. On the Enterprise plan, owners can also control auto-updates, workspace folders, local MCP servers, and desktop extensions, and block other accounts, in Organization settings without MDM. See Enterprise configuration for Claude Desktop.

Endpoint detection and response (EDR) sensor

Your device management (MDM) tool

Runs your EDR sensor inside the VM on a user’s computer (beta). It doesn’t cover the cloud sandbox, because Anthropic manages that virtual machine. See Run your EDR sensor in Claude Cowork.

Identity settings carry over unchanged. Members sign in to Claude as members of your organization, and your SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning, and tenant restrictions apply. The new unified Claude experience adds no separate sign-in.

For recommended Security settings and architecture, see Unified Claude and Cowork security best practices.

Data retention and deletion

  • Conversations. Conversations are kept until the member deletes them or according to your organization’s custom data retention setting if you’ve set one (minimum 30 days). See custom data retention. Conversations in a project are deleted with the project, once deleted by the user or once the project and all its conversations have been inactive for the project’s retention period. The period is measured from the most recent activity in the conversation or in any cloud session Claude started from it.
  • Cloud sessions started from a conversation. When a conversation is deleted, whether by a member, by deleting its project, or under your retention period, the cloud sessions Claude started in it are deleted too, including their transcripts. Deletion finishes in the background after the conversation is removed.
  • Memory. Account memory is covered by your custom data retention setting for chats, and project memory is deleted when the project is deleted, including by your project data retention period. After moving to the new experience, the memory will be moved to a new memory system and the old memory may be deleted 14 days later, or sooner if it’s past the data retention period.
  • Artifacts. Artifacts, including those Claude creates in conversations, follow your retention periods for private and shared artifacts, or your period for all data, not the conversation’s. These periods don’t delete artifacts published with a public link. Some artifacts, such as Research reports and artifacts in some older conversations, are deleted with their conversation instead.
  • Files Claude gives you. Almost all files (like documents or spreadsheets) that Claude gives you in a conversation on or after October 8, 2026 are deleted with it, including under your retention period, unless another conversation or project in your organization uses them. Older files may remain after their conversation is deleted.
  • Not deleted with a conversation. Custom data retention doesn’t cover:
    • Cowork cloud sessions a member starts directly, including in a project. These are kept until the member deletes them.
    • Scheduled tasks and their runs, including tasks created from a conversation. These keep running after that conversation is deleted. To stop them from running, turn off Scheduled tasks.
    • Cowork history stored on a member’s computer.
    • Memory of members who have left your organization.
    • Transcripts and memory kept by Claude Code (including Claude Code on the web), Claude Tag, and other products outside chat and Cowork.

Deletion happens after the period ends rather than at an exact moment, and deleted data is removed from our back-end systems. As with chat, we may retain content flagged by our trust and safety systems or as required by law. See How long do you store my organization’s data?

Manage access and spend

  • Pricing stays usage-based, and the spend controls you have today apply.
  • Spend limits can be set at the organization, group, and member level.
  • Usage analytics break out chat, Cowork, and the new unified Claude experience.
  • Models: The model allowlist you set applies to both chat and agentic work in the new unified Claude experience.

Usage and analytics

The new unified Claude experience gets its own line in your reports. When a member has access to the new unified Claude experience, their chat and Cowork usage is reported under Chat and Cowork unified, not under Chat or Cowork. Think of it as a new folder for the same work: only where the usage is filed changes, so moving usage to this line doesn’t change how it’s counted or billed.

How usage is counted
  • Counting follows each member. Usage counts toward the new unified Claude experience if the member has access to it when the usage happens. If you turn it on for some roles first, your reports can show Chat, Cowork, and Chat and Cowork unified on the same day.
  • It covers chat and Cowork. A member’s chats, their cloud sessions, and their use of the Cowork desktop app count toward the new unified Claude experience.
  • Other products keep their own line. For example, Claude Code and Claude in Chrome usage is still reported under those products.
  • Past usage stays where it is. Data for the new unified Claude experience starts the day a member first gets access. Usage from before then stays under Chat or Cowork. If you turn the new unified Claude experience off, past unified usage keeps its Chat and Cowork unified label, and new usage goes back to Chat and Cowork.
  • Include it when you add things up. When you add up spend, tokens, or messages for Chat and Cowork, include Chat and Cowork unified too. Otherwise your Chat and Cowork numbers will seem to drop as members move over. For the number of people, use the overall active users count rather than adding products together, since one person can be active in more than one.
In the analytics dashboard

A page of its own. Admins who can view analytics will find a Chat and Cowork unified page under Apps. It shows daily active users.

Across the dashboard. You can pick “Chat and Cowork unified” in the Active users, Active members, Total spend, and Spend by model charts. The See all members table on the Overview page has a “Messages in Chat and Cowork unified” column. The Top connectors and Top skills cards don’t include it yet.

Who sees it. The page appears for every organization that can turn on the new unified Claude experience, whether or not it is on yet.

Give it a day or two. New activity can take up to two days to show up.

In the APIs

Your keys already work. If you already use these APIs, your existing access keys work. If your scripts check responses against a fixed list of fields or products, add the new ones.

Cost and Usage API. Tokens and spend for the new unified Claude experience are reported under the product value chat_cowork_unified. You can filter to it with products[]. The chat and cowork values still work, and cover usage from members who didn’t have the new unified Claude experience at the time.

Analytics API. Member, skill, and connector rows have a chat_cowork_unified_metrics object with two parts: chat, for chat activity, and sessions, for cloud sessions and the Cowork desktop app. Daily summaries add daily, weekly, and monthly active user counts for the new unified Claude experience, such as chat_cowork_unified_daily_active_user_count.

What members see

Members with usage-based seats see their own usage of the new unified Claude experience on their usage page, listed as Chat and Cowork unified.

Unified smart report and analytics chat

To learn how to create a smart report, refer to Get started with smart reports. When choosing products to run the report for, choose “Chat and Cowork unified” to run the report against the new unified Claude experience.

Efficient mode for the new unified Claude experience

When on, org members can use only Sonnet and Haiku models in the new unified Claude experience, and new sessions start on Claude Sonnet 5.5 at low effort. Other products aren’t affected. As lower-cost models become available, Anthropic may update the default model and effort level to keep the best balance of performance and cost.

How to access it: Owners can turn it on for the whole org on the Models page, or for specific custom roles on each role’s Models tab.

Current limitations

  • ZDR, HIPAA, and CMEK. The new unified Claude experience isn’t available to organizations with zero data retention, the HIPAA-ready configuration, or customer-managed encryption keys. These organizations keep using chat and Cowork as they do today, and admins can’t turn on Chat and Cowork unified. HIPAA support is expected after general availability; CMEK support is planned for a later release. If your organization turns on CMEK after turning on the new experience, it becomes unavailable.

Set up and manage the new unified Claude experience for your Team organization

The new unified Claude experience brings chat and Cowork together on web, desktop, and mobile. Users no longer choose between chat and Cowork before they start. Every chat starts the same way, and when a task needs to run code or work with files, Claude continues the same chat in an Anthropic-managed cloud environment and returns the finished work for review.

This article explains how Team plan owners turn on the new unified Claude experience, which settings apply to it, and how to manage its cost.

The new unified Claude experience is available on Team plans, where it appears in admin settings as Chat and Cowork unified. It turns on by default on December 1, 2026, unless an owner keeps it off.

How the new unified Claude experience works

  • One conversation, two modes. A chat moves into a Cowork cloud session when a task needs it. Users aren’t asked to switch modes.
  • Longer tasks run in an isolated cloud environment. Each chat that needs one gets its own virtual machine, managed by Anthropic. After a few minutes idle, the virtual machine is stopped and its disk is saved as an encrypted snapshot. The environment expires 30 days after it was created.
  • Work moves across devices. A task started on the web can be picked up on desktop or mobile.
  • Local access stays optional. Through Claude Desktop, users can link their computers so Claude can work with local folders and applications.

Before you begin

The new unified Claude experience requires Cloud code execution and file creation to be on for your organization, since longer tasks run remotely.

It doesn’t require Cowork or Cowork in the cloud to be on.

The new unified Claude experience isn’t available yet for organizations that use zero data retention (ZDR). Learn more in Current limitations below.

Turn on the new unified Claude experience

For your whole organization
  • Sign in to Claude as an Owner or Primary Owner.
  • Go to Organization settings > Capabilities.
  • Turn on Chat and Cowork unified.
  • Ask users to refresh the Claude app if they don’t see the new experience right away.

Scheduled tasks and session history keep working after the change. You don’t need to update or recreate anything.

If you take no action
  • December 1, 2026: The new unified Claude experience turns on by default for your organization. To keep it off, select “Keep disabled” in Organization settings > Capabilities before then. If Cloud code execution and file creation is off, there’s no notice and nothing turns on. After December 1, the new experience turns on as soon as you turn that setting on. If you already turned Chat and Cowork unified on or off, that choice stays. New Team organizations already start with it on.
  • February 1, 2027: The separate chat and Cowork experience is retired. Any users still on it move to the new unified Claude experience automatically.

These dates don’t apply to organizations with zero data retention.

The separate chat and Cowork experience isn’t planned to get new features, apart from new model launches. New features are planned only for the new unified Claude experience, so we recommend starting your move now.
