Application: claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com, anthropic.com
Action: Inject Header
Header Name: anthropic-allowed-org-ids
Header Value:
TLS Inspection: Required
3. Test your configuration

From restricted network, test with your org’s API key:

curl [api.anthropic.com](https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages) \
  -H "x-api-key: $CLAUDE_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-6","max_tokens":1024,"messages":
 [{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'

Error responses

Access blocked

When a user’s organization isn’t on the allowlist, they receive a 403 error:

{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "permission_error",
    "message": "Access restricted by network policy. Contact IT Administrator.",
    "error_code": "tenant_restriction_violation"
  }
}
Header configuration errors

If your proxy sends the headers incorrectly, requests fail with a 400 status and one of these messages:

  • Multiple anthropic-allowed-org-ids headers: A header name appeared more than once on the same request. Configure your proxy to overwrite each header rather than append a duplicate.
  • Malformed anthropic-allowed-org-ids headers: The ;n=K value is invalid, a declared continuation slot is missing or extra, or the total allowlist exceeds 500 UUIDs.

Supported proxy platforms

  • Cato Networks (Tenant Restriction policy)
  • Cloudflare Zero Trust / Gateway (HTTP policy, add custom request headers)
  • Island (header injection in Island Enterprise Browser, Island Extension, and Secure Web Gateway)
  • Netskope (Header Insertion rules)
  • Palo Alto Prisma Access (SaaS App Management)
  • Zscaler ZIA (Cloud App Control policies)
  • Generic HTTPS proxies with header injection capability

Use cases

Scenario

Header Value

Single Organization

&lt;your-org-uuid>

Multiple Organizations (Partners)

&lt;org-uuid-1>,&lt;org-uuid-2>

Security benefits

  • Data Loss Prevention: Block personal account usage from corporate networks.
  • Compliance: Enforce data residency and access policies.
  • Shadow IT Control: Prevent unauthorized Claude usage.
  • Audit Trail: Complete visibility into access attempts.

Backward compatibility

  • No impact to networks without tenant restrictions configured.
  • Standard authentication continues for unmanaged networks.
  • Existing API key authentication remains unchanged.

Export your organization’s data

Organization data exports are only available to Team and Enterprise plan Primary Owners. Data exports include conversation data and the user data for your organization. Primary Owners and Owners can also let users export their own data. Learn more in the Let users export their own data section below.

If you’re an individual Claude user on a Free, Pro, Max, or Ultra plan looking to export your data, see Export your Claude data.

Primary Owners of Team and Enterprise plans can export organization data from Organization settings > Data and privacy on the web app or Claude Desktop.

Important: Data exports don’t include the Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or PDF files that Claude creates. Users can download these files from the chat while they’re available. Enterprise organizations using the Compliance API may also be able to retrieve them. Exports also don’t include security center attestation data.

Follow these steps to export your organization’s data:

  • Click on your initials in the lower left corner of your account.
  • Select “Organization settings” from the menu.
  • Click “Data and privacy” to open that section.
  • Click on the “Export Data” button.

Once the export has been processed, you will receive a download link via email.

Important: Messages, files, and projects deleted from your account, either manually by individual users or via enterprise retention settings, will not be included in data exports initiated after the deletion.

Please note:

  • There may be a small delay while the export is generated.
  • The email will be sent to the address associated with your account.
  • You must be signed in to your account to download your data using this link.
  • The download link will expire 24 hours after it’s created, and it may work only once, so download the file right away.
  • If your link expires or won’t open, you can request a new one by repeating the export process.

If you’re an Enterprise Primary Owner looking to export audit logs, see How to access audit logs.

Let users export their own data

Owners and Primary Owners can let users in your organization export their own chats without exporting the whole organization.

To turn this on:

  • Navigate to Organization settings > Data and privacy.
  • In the “Data management” section, turn on “Allow members to export their own data.”

Once the setting is on, users export their data from Settings > Privacy in Claude on the web or Claude Desktop. Exports aren’t available in Claude for iOS or Claude for Android. Each export covers the user’s own chats and doesn’t include the contents of uploaded files. Learn more about exporting your Claude data.

Note: Primary Owners don’t see the personal “Export data” button, even when this setting is on. These roles export the whole organization’s data using the steps above.

HIPAA-ready Enterprise plans

This feature is available for Enterprise plans only (both self-serve and sales-assisted).

We offer a HIPAA-ready version of Claude that is available for organizations on Enterprise plans that choose to process protected health information (PHI) through Claude. This article explains what the offering includes, which features are available, and how to get started.

Overview

The HIPAA-ready Enterprise offering is designed for healthcare providers, health plans, healthcare data processors, and their business associates who are subject to HIPAA requirements. This offering includes a Business Associate Agreement (BAA), functionality, and safeguards designed to support an organization’s HIPAA compliance requirements.

Who is this for?

This offering is designed for HIPAA-covered entities and their business associates, including:

  • Healthcare providers (e.g., hospitals, clinics, physicians)
  • Health plans and insurers
  • Healthcare data processors
  • Business associates that handle PHI on behalf of covered entities
  • Other HIPAA regulated entities

If you’re unsure whether your organization benefits from a HIPAA-ready product, ask yourself: will you be processing protected health information through Claude? If yes, you need the HIPAA-ready offering with a BAA.

Feature availability

The HIPAA-ready Enterprise offering includes many of the features available on standard Enterprise plans—but enabling HIPAA doesn’t bring every feature under your BAA. Features fall into three categories: covered by your BAA, available but not covered, and disabled. PHI should only be processed through covered features, so it’s important for administrators to know which features fall in which category and to configure their workspace accordingly. The Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities on the Anthropic Trust Center lists every feature’s status and is the authoritative source.

Important: Enabling HIPAA alone doesn’t bring Claude Code or Cowork under your BAA. The Primary Owner must also apply the HIPAA configuration to Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode). This configuration is currently only available to organizations with an Anthropic account team. Claude Code (local mode) is Claude Code in the terminal and in the Code tab of Claude Desktop. Cowork (local mode) is Cowork in Claude Desktop.

  • Before the Primary Owner applies the configuration: Cowork is available but not covered under your BAA. Claude Code is covered only with zero data retention (ZDR) enabled, which is available on qualified accounts only. Without ZDR, Claude Code is also available but not covered. Don’t use PHI with a product that isn’t covered.
  • After the Primary Owner applies the configuration: Your BAA covers Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode). Cloud features such as Claude Code cloud sessions, Claude Code Remote Control, and Cowork in the cloud aren’t available. The Primary Owner can’t remove the configuration.

Learn how to get the configuration and how to prepare in Use Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode) on a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan.

Additional resources

For detailed implementation requirements and technical specifications, review the Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities on the Anthropic Trust Center. You can download the Implementation Guide directly during the setup flow.

Note: You’ll need to request access to view the Implementation Guide. Requests from domains matching existing customer accounts are approved automatically.

Get started

Eligible Enterprise organizations can enable HIPAA directly from organization settings—no sales or legal cycle required. The Business Associate Agreement (BAA) is included in the flow as click-to-accept, so there’s no separate document to sign and return. Clicking “Accept and Enable HIPAA” constitutes acceptance of the BAA.

Eligibility

You can enable HIPAA from organization settings if your organization is on an Enterprise plan. Team plans and individual plans (Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra) can’t enable HIPAA.

Only the Primary Owner of the organization can accept the BAA and enable HIPAA. Other Owners or Admins can’t complete this flow on the org’s behalf. If you’re an admin but not the Primary Owner of the Enterprise organization, ask your Primary Owner to sign in and complete enablement.

Before you begin

Two things to know up front:

  • Enabling HIPAA resets certain settings across your organization. Some configurations return to defaults as part of the transition to a HIPAA-ready state. The onboarding modal and the Implementation Guide (downloadable during the flow) detail what changes.
  • This is a one-way decision. Once HIPAA is enabled and the BAA is accepted, the change can’t be reversed from organization settings.

You must review the BAA and the Implementation Guide before accepting, as this is an irreversible organization transition.

Note: The BAA offered through the self-serve flow is a standard agreement and can’t be modified.

Enable HIPAA
  • Sign in to Claude as the Primary Owner and go to Organization settings > Data and privacy.
  • Go to HIPAA Compliance.
  • Click “Enable” to open the consent flow.
  • Download the Business Associate Agreement, review it, then click “Next.”
  • Download the Implementation Guide, review it, then click “Next.”
  • Click “Accept and enable HIPAA.”
Confirmation

Once enabled, you’ll see a checkmark in the HIPAA Compliance section of organization settings, confirming your organization has been configured to process PHI through Claude in accordance with HIPAA. If you don’t see this checkmark, your organization isn’t enabled. Enabling HIPAA alone doesn’t bring Claude Code or Cowork under your BAA. The Primary Owner must also apply the HIPAA configuration to Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode). See Use Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode) on a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan.

The onboarding modal will guide you through next steps for your team.

For help with the BAA, the Implementation Guide, or post-enablement questions, reach out to your Anthropic account team or our support team.

If you have an existing API BAA

If your organization signed a BAA for Claude API usage before December 2, 2025, that agreement only covers API usage—it does not extend to the HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan. To add this Enterprise plan access, you’ll need to sign a new BAA with your account team.

BAAs signed after December 2, 2025 can cover both API usage and the Enterprise plan under a single agreement.

If you use the Claude API, learn more about HIPAA-ready Claude API access and how to set it up.

Inference hooks overview

Inference hooks lets your compliance team inspect and enforce policy on every prompt, tool call response, and uploaded file text before it reaches Claude.

Inference hooks are generally available to Enterprise plans and cover Claude, Claude Code, Cowork, and all other Claude Enterprise products. They can be turned on and managed by Owners and Primary Owners.

When you turn on inference hooks, Claude sends every prompt to a server you host before it starts generating a response. It also sends every tool call to that server before the tool runs. Your server checks the prompt against your policy, then answers allow or deny. Claude only continues once it has that answer.

Because this check happens inside Claude’s infrastructure rather than on someone’s device, it doesn’t rely on anything installed on employees’ devices. One setup covers your whole organization: Claude, Claude Code, Cowork, and more, including tool calls made through skills, plugins, and connected tools.

Common uses include data loss prevention, real-time transcript archival, and enforcing your own organization’s policies.

Technical documentation

For the full technical documentation, including configuring and monitoring the hook, implementing an endpoint, verifying request signatures, and the API reference, see Inference hooks.

Restrict access to Claude with IP allowlisting

IP allowlisting is available in public beta for Enterprise plans and Claude Platform organizations.

An IP allowlist limits access to Claude to the IP addresses your organization approves. Owners on Enterprise plans and Admins on Claude Platform can set up and manage their IP allowlist themselves, without going through Anthropic. For full documentation and setup guides, see IP allowlisting on Claude API Docs.

Important: Artifacts shared outside your organization aren’t limited by your allowlist. Learn more about managing sharing outside your organization.

Review your organization’s security posture with the security center

The security center (beta) is a page in Organization settings for Claude Enterprise. It shows how your organization’s Claude settings compare with Anthropic’s recommended configuration across chats, Claude Cowork, and Claude Code, so your security and IT teams can review them in one place. It also shows which settings are new or recently changed.

For each control, the security center shows the current value, the recommended value where there is one, whether the control passed, and where to change the setting. It’s built for the people who own your organization’s Claude configuration: Claude Owners, and the IT and security teams who review how Claude is set up.

Security center is in beta for Claude Enterprise organizations.

Open the security center

  • In Claude, open your account menu and choose “Organization settings.”
  • Select “Security posture.”

What the page shows

  • Control groups: controls are grouped into Org, chats, Cowork, and Claude Code, each with its own count of controls that passed. Each group covers both Organization settings and settings you manage through device management or Claude Code managed settings.
  • For each security control: its current value, its recommended value where there is one, and its status: Passed (matches the recommendation), Failed (doesn’t match, with why it matters and where to change it), Not attested (needs a person to confirm it), or Shown for information (reported, not judged).
  • Trends over time: how your results have moved.
  • New and recently changed: markers on controls that were recently added or whose value recently changed.

Additional capabilities

  • Adoption and activity: figures on how your members use Claude, shown beside the controls.
  • Roles and connectors: what each of your custom roles allows across connectors and Claude features. Custom roles apply only to members whose role type is Custom.
  • Attestation: for controls the security center can’t check, such as settings in your device management tool or network proxy, record the current state of each control, accept risks, and flag issues in one place. Security center shows who attested and when.
  • Download a report: in a web browser, select “Download report” and save it as a PDF to share with auditors. It marks which controls were checked automatically and which an Owner confirmed, and it isn’t a security certification.
  • Compliance API and programmatic data: when Compliance API is enabled, you can read the data programmatically to bring it into your security tools. When a control’s status changes, an event is sent to your organization’s activity feed.

Frequently asked questions

Does the security center change any of my settings?

No. It’s view-only. You change each setting on its own page in Organization settings.

Why does a control say “Check manually?”

The setting is managed outside Claude’s admin settings, for example in your device management tool or Claude Code managed settings, so the security center can’t read it. You can attest to it instead.

Who can see the security center?

Owners and the Primary Owner. Admins and users can’t open it.

Important: Security center is guidance, not a guarantee. Its checks compare your settings with Anthropic’s recommended configuration, and neither the page nor its PDF report is a security certification. Results Claude checks automatically are labeled separately from controls an Owner confirms by hand.

Run your endpoint detection and response (EDR) sensor in Claude Cowork on Claude Desktop

When Claude Cowork runs on a user’s computer, either on its own or as part of the new unified Claude experience that brings chat and Cowork together, it runs shell commands and code in an isolated virtual machine (VM). The endpoint detection and response (EDR) sensor already on that computer can’t see inside the VM. This article shows IT and security admins how to run the sensor inside the VM, so activity in the VM reports to the console your security team already uses.

Running an EDR sensor in Cowork is available in beta for Team and Enterprise plans. It’s available for Claude Desktop on macOS and Windows, and for Claude Desktop connected to Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, or Microsoft Foundry.

Important: This covers only the VM on the user’s computer. Cowork sessions in the cloud run on Anthropic’s servers, and you can’t install a sensor there.

How it works

  • Each time the Cowork VM starts, Claude Desktop copies your vendor’s sensor package into the VM and checks its signature against the approved key of the vendor you named.
  • If the signature is valid, Claude runs the vendor’s install script inside the VM, at most once per VM start. If the setting isn’t set, nothing is installed.
  • The sensor connects to your vendor’s cloud and reports activity, the same way it does from the rest of the computer. The sensor can send telemetry and data out of the VM, outside the Cowork network allowlist.

The VM starts the first time something needs it, usually when a user opens Cowork, and runs until Claude quits or the user signs out.

Supported vendors

Claude Desktop only installs a sensor package signed with the key of an approved EDR vendor.

Approved vendors:

  • CrowdStrike
  • Evoke Security
  • Neo
  • Palo Alto Networks
  • Pluto Security
  • SentinelOne
  • Tanium

If your vendor isn’t listed, ask them to apply using the form in For EDR vendors below. If you have an Anthropic account team, let them know you need it.

Before you start

You’ll need:

  • macOS: Claude Desktop 4.4212.0 or later
  • Windows: The .msix build of Claude Desktop, 4.4212.0 or later, on Windows 10 or 11 with hardware virtualization and the Virtual Machine Platform feature turned on
  • Device management: An MDM tool for macOS, or a way to set registry policy on Windows, such as Group Policy or Intune

Then follow your EDR vendor’s setup guidance. Each vendor provides its own files and instructions.

Frequently asked questions

Does the integration cover Cowork sessions in the cloud?

No. Some Cowork tasks run in a cloud VM that Anthropic hosts, and your EDR sensor can’t be installed there. The integration covers only the local VM on the user’s computer.

What can the sensor see?

The sensor can see activity and content inside the VM, which can include prompts, files, and Claude’s responses. It sends data to your EDR vendor. Anthropic doesn’t receive or control that data.

Does the integration cost extra?

Anthropic doesn’t charge extra for the integration during the beta. Your EDR vendor may charge for the sensor, so contact them for pricing details.

What happens if I remove the MDM settings?

Removing the settings doesn’t remove a sensor that’s already installed. Claude stops running the package at later VM starts.

How do sensor updates work?

Your vendor maintains the package. The signature covers only the package file, not updates the sensor downloads later. Signatures expire within two years, so you’ll deploy a re-signed package from your vendor.

For EDR vendors

If you’re an EDR vendor and want your sensor to run in the Cowork VM, apply to join the integration.

Terms

Your organization chooses the security vendor. Your organization uses the EDR Software under its own agreement with that vendor.

The EDR Software is a Third Party Feature under your agreement with Anthropic. It is not part of Anthropic’s Services.

The EDR Software can see activity and content inside the virtual machine. This can include prompts, files and Claude’s responses. It sends data to the vendor. Anthropic does not receive or control that data, and the vendor does not handle it on Anthropic’s behalf.

Your organization is responsible for the EDR Software. This includes testing it before you deploy it and again after any update to Claude or to the EDR Software. Anthropic is not responsible for claims that arise from a failure to test.

Your organization is responsible for claims that arise from the EDR Software, as described in your agreement with Anthropic.

Use Claude Code (local mode) and Claude Cowork (local mode) on a HIPAA-ready Enterprise plan

The HIPAA configuration is an organization setting on Enterprise plans. It brings local Claude Code and Claude Cowork sessions under your Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with Anthropic. Cloud sessions, including Claude Code sessions in the cloud and Cowork in the cloud, aren’t covered. This article calls them Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode). They run in one of these places:

  • Claude Code in the terminal
  • Claude Code in the Code section of Claude Desktop
  • Cowork in Claude Desktop

With the configuration applied, members can use both products with protected health information (PHI), on the conditions in Check what your BAA covers. Applying it also turns off certain features across your organization.

Available on Enterprise plans with an Anthropic account team. Only the Primary Owner can apply the HIPAA configuration.

This article is for the Primary Owner, who applies the configuration, and for any Owner who helps decide whether to apply it, prepare for it, and confirm it.

“HIPAA-ready” means the product is configured to support your HIPAA obligations under the BAA. Compliance remains your organization’s responsibility.

Note:

  • If your organization hasn’t enabled HIPAA, start with HIPAA-ready Enterprise plans. Enabling HIPAA brings chat under your BAA. That step alone doesn’t bring Claude Code (local mode) or Cowork (local mode) under your BAA.
  • If you prepare members’ computers, see Set up Claude Code (local mode) for a HIPAA-ready organization and Set up Cowork (local mode) for a HIPAA-ready organization.
  • If you want to check whether a specific feature is covered under your BAA, see the list of Eligible Services in the Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities and Business Associate Agreements (BAA) for Commercial Customers.

Check what your BAA covers

After you apply the HIPAA configuration, your BAA covers each product in the table, on the condition in the second column. Applying the configuration turns off Cowork and the Code section of Claude Desktop, even if they were on, so an Owner has to turn each one on afterward.

Product

Covered under your BAA when

Claude Code in the terminal

Members sign in with their Claude Enterprise account, and Claude Code connects directly to Anthropic, not through a cloud provider or gateway

Claude Code in the Code section of Claude Desktop

An Owner has turned on the “Desktop” toggle in Organization settings > Claude Code

Cowork in Claude Desktop

An Owner has turned on the “Enable for your organization” toggle in Organization settings > Cowork

You don’t need zero data retention (ZDR) to apply the configuration. If your organization has ZDR for Claude Code, see Replace ZDR with the configuration.

Products and features your BAA doesn’t cover

Keep PHI out of these products and features. Your BAA doesn’t cover them, even with the configuration applied:

  • The Claude Code extensions for VS Code and JetBrains, which keep working after you apply the configuration
  • Any feature labeled beta or research preview
  • Claude Code sessions that connect through a cloud provider such as Amazon Bedrock, an LLM gateway, or a custom base URL
  • Claude Code sessions that use a Claude Console API key, unless the Claude Console organization has ZDR enabled
  • Connectors, MCP servers, plugins, desktop extensions, Claude in Chrome, and skills, including after an Owner turns them on
  • Cloud and remote features such as Claude Code cloud sessions, which the configuration makes unavailable

Ask your IT team to deploy managed settings, a policy file on each computer that directs members to sign in with a Claude Enterprise account and refuses cloud providers and gateways. For a full list of Eligible Services, please review the Implementation Guide and Business Associate Agreements (BAA) for Commercial Customers.

Ask Anthropic to turn on the HIPAA configuration

You apply the configuration with the “Apply HIPAA configuration” button in Organization settings > Data and privacy. The button is grayed out until Anthropic turns it on for your organization. Ask your Anthropic account team to turn it on. The HIPAA configuration is only available to organizations with an Anthropic account team at this time. Anthropic Support can’t turn it on for your organization.

See Coverage until you apply the configuration and Business Associate Agreements (BAA) for Commercial Customers for what your BAA covers if you haven’t applied it.

Coverage until you apply the configuration

Until you apply the configuration, members can still use Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode) where an Owner has them turned on, but your BAA may not cover their use. Coverage differs for organizations with and without zero data retention (ZDR) for Claude Code:

  • Without ZDR for Claude Code: Your BAA doesn’t cover Claude Code or Cowork, so don’t use them to process PHI.
  • With ZDR for Claude Code: Your BAA covers Claude Code through ZDR. It doesn’t cover Cowork, so don’t use Cowork to process PHI.

Your account team can tell you whether your organization has ZDR for Claude Code.

Replace ZDR with the configuration

The configuration is meant to replace ZDR for Claude Code (local mode). Applying it doesn’t turn ZDR off. Don’t apply the configuration if you wish to keep your existing access through ZDR.

If you have ZDR enabled for Claude Code within Claude for Enterprise, email your account team for help switching to the HIPAA configuration.

Once ZDR is removed, Anthropic keeps Claude Code data under standard retention, as it does for your organization’s chat data.

Prepare your organization

Complete these tasks before you apply the configuration.

Review what changes for members

The table shows the changes members are most likely to notice, and what to do about each one before you apply the configuration. The Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities and Business Associate Agreements (BAA) for Commercial Customers list the Eligible Services under your BAA.

What changes

What to do before you apply

Cowork, the Code section of Claude Desktop, skills, and Claude in Chrome turn off, even if an Owner had turned them on

List the ones you want back and who approves each one

Every other setting that enabling HIPAA turns off by default turns off again, including chat settings

List the settings an Owner has turned on since you enabled HIPAA

Each connector turns off, and its tool permissions change to Blocked, unless an Owner accepted the terms when they added or enabled it

Record each connector’s tool permissions, because turning the connector back on doesn’t restore them

The built-in GitHub integration turns off

Note whether you want it back

Each desktop extension is removed from your organization’s allowlist, unless an Owner accepted the terms when they added it

List the extensions you want to add again

Within minutes, members can’t start Claude Code cloud sessions or use Cowork in the cloud. Sessions that are already running stop. Members will lose access to them.

Ask members to finish that work and save what they need

Claude Code Remote Control and Claude Tag aren’t available. Claude Design turns off until an Owner turns it on

Ask members who use them to finish that work

Computer access in Claude Cowork isn’t available for sessions and scheduled tasks that run in the cloud

Ask members who use them to finish that work, and tell them that scheduled tasks in Cowork (local mode) still run on their computer

Approvals that members gave to scheduled tasks in Cowork and the Code section of Claude Desktop expire

Tell members to expect to approve their scheduled tasks again

Chat uses the same connectors, skills, and Claude in Chrome settings, so when these turn off, they turn off in chat too.

Have your team review the terms

When you apply the configuration, you accept the BAA and confirm that you reviewed the Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities, which includes a list of Eligible Services under your BAA. Ask your legal and compliance teams to review both documents before you apply the configuration.

Ask your IT team to prepare computers

Ask your IT team to follow Set up Claude Code (local mode) for a HIPAA-ready organization. If members use Cowork, ask the team to follow Set up Cowork (local mode) for a HIPAA-ready organization too. They update Claude Code and Claude Desktop to the latest versions, allow network access to Anthropic’s servers, and deploy managed settings and the Claude Desktop policy.

The update matters because once the configuration is applied, Anthropic’s servers reject requests from versions older than the minimum.

Choose a time and tell members

Apply the configuration at a quiet time for your organization because Cowork, the Code section of Claude Desktop, and some connectors stay off until an Owner turns them on. Keep an Owner available afterward, and plan time to turn on each connector separately.

Tell members the date and time, which features turn off, and which ones you plan to turn back on.

Apply the HIPAA configuration

To apply the configuration, you must be the Primary Owner and have a verified email address. Other Owners and Admins can’t apply it, because applying it includes accepting the BAA for your organization.

The configuration applies to your existing Claude Enterprise organization, the same one your members use for chat, not to a separate account. It applies to Claude Code and Cowork together, and to every member.

Warning: When you apply the HIPAA configuration, certain features start turning off across your organization as soon as you confirm. An Owner can turn some features back on, but cloud features such as Claude Code cloud sessions stay unavailable.

To apply the configuration:

  • Sign in to Claude as the Primary Owner and go to Organization settings > Data and privacy.
  • In the “Compliance” section, find the row for Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode).
  • Select “Apply HIPAA configuration.” A dialog opens.
  • In the dialog, review what changes, then download the Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities, and the BAA if your organization has none on file. The “Apply HIPAA configuration” button in the dialog stays grayed out until you download them. Selecting it accepts Anthropic’s updated BAA.
  • Select “Apply HIPAA configuration” to confirm. A message confirms that the configuration is applied.

If the button is grayed out, check that you’re signed in as the Primary Owner and that your email address is verified. If it’s still grayed out, ask Anthropic to turn it on.

Turn features back on

Cowork, the Code section of Claude Desktop, skills, and Claude in Chrome are off after you apply the configuration, and so is each connector whose terms no Owner had accepted. An Owner turns on the ones your organization approved. The Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities and Business Associate Agreements (BAA) for Commercial Customers list the Eligible Services under your BAA.

Turning a feature on doesn’t change whether your BAA covers it.

Connectors take more steps, because you turn on each one separately. Go to Organization settings > Connectors, open the connector, select “Enable” in the banner, select the checkbox to accept the terms, and click “Continue.” Then set the connector’s tool permissions again.

Confirm the configuration is applied

Ask members to restart Claude Code and Claude Desktop, so that both get the configuration right away. Without a restart, a running Claude Code session gets it within about an hour. Claude Desktop might not get it until a member restarts or reloads the app.

Organization settings, Claude Code, and Claude Desktop each show the configuration once it’s applied:

  • Organization settings: Go to Organization settings > Data and privacy. Confirm that the row for Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode) says they’re HIPAA configured for this organization, and shows the date you applied the configuration.
  • Claude Code: Ask a member to run /status in a session. Confirm that the Status tab lists HIPAA on the Organization configuration line.
  • Claude Desktop: Confirm that the title bar shows a HIPAA configured label. On a Mac, open the sidebar to see it.

Tell members not to process PHI until they see HIPAA in /status, or the HIPAA configured label, on their own computer.

If either one is missing on a member’s computer, ask your IT team to follow Confirm the configuration on a computer, which lists the likely causes in order. For the Claude Desktop label, see The HIPAA configured label is missing. If it’s still missing, contact your account team.

Manage data on members’ computers

Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode) store session data, such as transcripts, on each member’s computer. Securing and deleting that data is your organization’s responsibility.

Removing a member from your organization deletes nothing on their computer, so wipe the computer when a member leaves. Keep full-disk encryption turned on.

Manage local session data lists where the data is stored, what Claude Code (local mode) and Claude Desktop delete automatically, and how to delete the rest. For Cowork data, see Manage Cowork data on each computer.

Monitor sessions

These tools show what happens in Claude Code (local mode) and Cowork (local mode). They differ in whether they include session content:

  • Compliance API: With the Compliance API turned on for your organization, Anthropic captures session activity and content from both products so that your organization can read it through the API. Sessions are readable for 30 days, or for your organization’s retention period if it’s shorter. While your organization has ZDR for Claude Code, Anthropic doesn’t capture Claude Code sessions.
  • Audit logs and data exports: Audit logs and data exports don’t include session content. The audit log records administrative changes, such as enabling HIPAA and applying the configuration.
  • OpenTelemetry: You can send events from both products to your own monitoring tools. The data you export is your organization’s responsibility. Set the destination for Cowork in Organization settings > Data and privacy > Monitoring. Your IT team sets the destination for Claude Code in managed settings.

Important: Cowork’s OpenTelemetry events can include prompt text, Claude’s responses, and tool inputs, so PHI in a session may reach your monitoring tools. Current versions of Claude Desktop only send metadata unless content capture is turned on, but some older versions send content such as prompt text and tool inputs by default. No organization setting turns that content off. Ask your IT team to set otlpContentCapture to [] so that every version that supports the policy sends metadata only, as described in Content capture. Metadata still includes the paths of connected folders, user email addresses, and API error messages, and an API error message can sometimes repeat part of the request. If these can contain PHI, filter or redact them at your collector.

Get help

For questions about the BAA, the Implementation Guide for HIPAA Entities, or the configuration, contact your Anthropic account team. If your organization doesn’t have an account team, contact our Support team. Do not include PHI in a support request.

Use Claude Security

Overview

Claude Security is a capability built into Claude that continuously watches your codebases for security vulnerabilities, tracks each finding until it is fixed, and suggests targeted patches for human review. It helps teams find and fix issues that traditional methods often miss.

Claude Security is available in beta for users on Enterprise plans.

Learn how to get started and how leading enterprises use the tool here: Getting started with Claude Security.

Claude Security allows you to:

  • Scan your codebase holistically — Claude Security understands how your code fits together, traces data flows across files and across the repositories in a project, and identifies complex, multi-component vulnerabilities and bugs that traditional rules-based scanners cannot detect.
  • Deep Scan — Create a project and connect up to eight repositories from GitHub or other Git providers. Claude reads the code, writes a threat model, and runs a deep baseline scan.
  • Continuous Scanning — Claude Security runs an efficient scan when new commits land, and surfaces any new findings for quick remediation.
  • Add what the code can’t show — Tell Claude how your code is deployed, who can reach it, and which risks you’ve accepted. Each project keeps this in a threat model, and Claude uses it to decide what to flag and how to rate it.
  • Validate findings — Every finding goes through multi-stage verification, with Claude critically reviewing its own findings before they’re surfaced. The result: fewer false positives, less noise.
  • Review and patch — Seamlessly move from a finding into a Claude Code session to generate a targeted fix. Resolve vulnerabilities quickly instead of growing a backlog.
  • Track fixes — Claude checks open findings against the code that changed and marks them fixed when the fix lands.
  • Integrate into your workflow — Read and resolve findings through the Claude Security API or the Claude Security connector (MCP) in Claude and Claude Code, and get a webhook when a new finding is added.
  • Control access — Share each project with a Full, Triage, or View role. Admins can decide who can create projects and who can view, triage, or manage all projects with RBAC.

Severities

Severity is assigned per finding based on how exploitable it is in your codebase, not the category itself—so the same category can land at different severities in different repos. Claude uses the project’s threat model to assess the severity.

Severity

Criteria

Typical example

Critical

Exploitable over the network by anyone, with no login, no action by a victim, and no special conditions. It lets the attacker both read and change data.

Unauthenticated remote code execution in an internet-facing service.

High

Serious impact, but short of Critical: the attacker needs a login or a victim’s action, or the damage is partial (for example, data can be read but not changed).

SQL injection behind a login that lets an attacker read and change data.

Medium

Limited impact (for example, a small amount of non-sensitive data), with one realistic precondition such as a login.

SQL injection behind a login that exposes only a few non-sensitive fields.

Low

Limited impact, and needs a login or network proximity plus special conditions outside the attacker’s control.

Timing side-channel requiring network proximity and thousands of requests.

Finding structure

Each finding contains the following fields:

  • Title — short descriptive name of the finding
  • Severity — Critical / High / Medium / Low
  • Category — finding type, with its CWE ID when one applies
  • Location — file path and line range, linked to the source. A finding can cite several files and repositories.
  • Status — Open or Resolved, with the date it was found.
  • Assignee — the person the finding is assigned to, if any
  • What Claude found — description of what the finding is and why it matters. It can include a diagram of the attack path.
  • How to fix — guidance on how to resolve it
  • Evidence — the files and line ranges Claude cites, grouped by repository, with the branch and commit that were scanned
  • How the attack works — how an attacker would reach and exploit the issue
  • Why Claude believes it — Claude’s assessment, covering the exploit scenario, its preconditions, and the impact
  • History — every change to the finding, newest first
  • Shown only if the finding was resolved:
    • Resolution — Marked fixed, Fixed by a merged pull request, or Dismissed as a false positive, an accepted risk, a duplicate, or for another reason
    • Triage note — optional

Frequently asked questions

Getting started

What do I need before I can use Claude Security?

An active Claude Enterprise plan and a seat that includes Claude Code for each Claude Security user. On seat-based Enterprise plans, usage credits must also be turned on. An owner whose seat includes Claude Code enables Claude Security in Organization settings > Claude Security. See the getting started guide for setup steps.

How do I give Claude Security access to my repositories?

For GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Server, an owner installs the Claude GitHub App and grants it access to the repositories you want to scan. For other Git providers, such as GitLab, Azure DevOps, and Bitbucket, enter the repository’s https address and an auth token that can read the repository. Write the address in lower case, with no user name, password, query or port, for example: https://gitlab.com/group/project.

Can I scan repositories that aren’t on GitHub?

Yes. Projects can be created with repositories hosted on GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Server, or repositories hosted on other Git servers with an auth token (including publicly accessible self-hosted Git servers).

Which IP addresses do I need to allow?

Use the Outbound IP addresses list for IP address allowlisting. If you use GitHub Enterprise Server or another Git provider, your instance must allow inbound traffic from these IP addresses so Claude Security can reach your repositories.

Does Claude Security support Zero Data Retention (ZDR)?

No. Anthropic may retain data where required by law or to address Usage Policy violations.

Does Claude Security work with customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK)?

No. Turning on customer-managed encryption keys turns off Claude Security for your organization.

What happens to my existing projects with the latest update?

We’re automatically moving existing projects to the new experience, and the earlier version will be retired on November 25, 2026. Your findings are copied to a new project, and the original is archived. You can no longer start scans or add schedules in the earlier version.

When we move a project that has no active scan schedule, it arrives paused. Its owner, or anyone with the Full role on it, can click “Resume scans” if they have access to the repository. Resuming turns on continuous monitoring: Claude reviews all the code in the project and keeps reviewing it, charged at token cost. A project that had a schedule on normally starts continuous monitoring by itself within a day or two after it moves, and is charged the same way. To stop it, the owner or anyone with the Full role can click “Pause scans” in the project’s menu. Some arrive paused instead, for example when another project already covers the same code, so check yours.

Once the earlier version is retired, you won’t be able to access it. If a project you own hasn’t moved yet, click “Move your projects” on the Claude Security home page. If you don’t see that button, or a project still hasn’t moved, contact your account team or Support.

Can I migrate my existing projects?

Yes, if you own the project and your role lets you create projects. Click “Move your projects” on the Claude Security home page. While the earlier version is still open, you can also open one project there and click “Move project”. Claude Security creates a new project, copies the findings to it, and archives the original. A move can’t be undone. The new project may start scanning right away, and setup and scans are charged at token cost. Most projects have already been moved automatically. GitHub Enterprise projects move with “Move your projects”, or we move them for you.

What comes with a project when it moves?

Findings come with their status, and dismissed or fixed findings keep their note. The owner, members, and sharing come too where possible. Scan history, the scan schedule, links to fix pull requests, the date a finding was first found, and who dismissed it aren’t copied. In the API, moved projects and findings have new IDs and are dated at the move, so a tool that imports findings may see them as new. A paused project has the status paused.

Why does a moved project have an owner or sharing I didn’t expect?

A move normally keeps both. If the owner has left your organization, the project goes to someone it was shared with, or to an organization owner or admin. To change it, the owner or someone with “Manage all projects” clicks “Share”, opens the role menu next to the new owner’s name, and clicks “Transfer ownership”. Members with “View all projects” can see moved projects that were private before, and their findings, even for repositories they can’t access on GitHub.

What changes for my webhooks?

A project’s webhooks are copied where possible. Slack webhooks need no change. Others get a new signing secret and Standard Webhooks signatures. A receiver that checks signatures refuses messages until you update it, and they’re dropped after a few retries. Open Webhooks, click “Rotate signing secret”, and copy the secret, which is shown once. Add it to your receiver with a Standard Webhooks check, and keep the old check while projects that haven’t moved still send to it. Turn the webhook on if it’s off, and click “Send test event”. Scan completed events are no longer sent, and finding IDs are now strings. Organization-wide webhooks aren’t copied: an organization owner can import them on the Webhooks page.

Continuous monitoring

How long does the first scan take?

Depending on the size of the repositories, the baseline scan may take several minutes or hours. You can leave the page while it runs. If you have enabled email notifications for Claude Security, you will receive an email when your project’s scan completes and it has new findings.

How often does Claude scan after the first scan?

Claude checks for new commits and scans changes regularly, based on their risk and complexity. There is no fixed schedule.

How long does a follow-up scan take?

Scan time varies based on the repository and the agent’s actions.

What does a follow-up scan read?

Claude checks for changes, reviews them, and intelligently determines the scan scope based upon risk, complexity and your scan effort. Depending upon your settings, scope, and how long it has been, Claude may choose a full or incremental scan. You can see in the Activity tab whether it has run a full or incremental scan with the specific changes scoped.

Why can two scans of the same code return different results?

Scans are stochastic by design. Unlike traditional static analyzers, Claude Security uses an agent that adapts its analysis to each run, reasoning over code context rather than applying fixed pattern matches. This enables the depth of analysis needed to catch logic-level vulnerabilities.

How should I set up a large repository or monorepo?

Set a folder scope on the repository rather than scanning the full repository, and exclude folders you don’t need covered. Claude can still pull context from the rest of the codebase as needed.

How many repositories can a project have?

Up to eight. A repository can be in scope, so Claude scans it and reports findings, or used for context only, so Claude reads it during scans but reports no findings in it. Both count toward the limit. Manage a project’s repositories on its Resources tab.

How do I tell Claude about my environment?

Open the project’s Resources tab to edit the threat model and add documents such as architecture docs. Claude uses them to decide what to flag and how to rate it.

Which models does Claude Security use?

Claude Security scans are powered by a Claude Mythos model. Users receive findings without direct model access. Each project’s chat with Claude uses a model your team picks from the ones your organization allows. Certain subcomponents of Claude Security may use other models when Mythos-class reasoning is not required, for example to enumerate a project directory.

Findings and fixes

How is severity assigned, and can I change it?

Claude rates each finding against the project’s threat model, which your team can edit and correct.

What if a finding describes an attack that isn’t possible in my environment?

Claude writes the threat model from your code, so it can miss deployment context and the patterns your company has accepted. In the project’s chat, tell Claude why the finding is wrong and ask it to update the threat model. Claude uses the threat model to decide what to flag and how to rate it.

How do I fix a finding?

Click “Fix” on a finding to open Claude Code and fix that specific vulnerability. Without Claude Code in the cloud, you copy a prompt into your own Claude Code. Claude will detect the code fixes in future scans and automatically resolve the finding. Additionally, you can always manually mark findings as fixed in the UI.

How does fix tracking work?

Claude re-checks findings when the code changes on the repository. Regardless if the finding was manually or automatically marked as fixed, Claude reopens the finding automatically if it later finds the issue is unresolved.

What happens when I dismiss a finding?

You can dismiss a finding as a false positive, an accepted risk, a duplicate, or for another reason, and add a triage note. A dismissed finding stays closed. When a later scan reports the same issue, Claude matches it to the dismissed finding and keeps it closed. You can reopen a dismissed finding yourself at any time.

Integrations and notifications

How do I export findings to my own tools?

To export findings into your own tracking and notification systems, use the Claude Security API, the Claude Security connector, or webhooks.

How do I use the Claude Security API?

Create a personal access token under Claude Security settings. A token acts as you: it can see and change only what you can. With the API, you can list and read projects and findings, resolve and reopen findings, and create and manage projects and their repositories.

What can the Claude Security connector (MCP) do?

With the Claude Security connector, Claude and Claude Code can list and read your projects and findings and resolve or reopen a finding when you ask.

How do I get notified when there is a new finding?

Create a webhook under Claude Security settings to push new-finding events into your own systems, such as Slack or Jira.

Access and sharing

How do admins control who can use Claude Security?

A member on a custom role needs both the Claude Security and the Claude Code capabilities. While Claude Security is in beta, the “All generally available” capability setting doesn’t include it. Admins can decide which RBAC roles can create projects and which can view, triage, or manage all projects by configuring the capabilities in custom roles.

How do I share a project, and what can each role do?

In a project, click “Share” to give members a role: Full (manage findings, settings, and who has access), Triage (view findings, update their status, and start fixes), or View. You can also share a project with your whole organization.

Pricing

How much does Claude Security cost?

Claude Security is charged at direct token cost only. There is no additional platform fee. Usage covers scans and other work Claude Security does in a project: writing a threat model, the project chat, and checking fixes.

How do I control and track what Claude Security costs?

You can set a separate spend limit for Claude Security. Open Usage in a project’s settings to see its cost for the month to date and per day.

Is there a launch offer for the updated Claude Security?

Yes, eligible Claude Enterprise organizations receive free usage credits up to $25,000 a month, for two months, through December 31, 2026. For organizations that already had Claude Enterprise on October 21, 2026, the first month ends on November 21 at 00:00 UTC and the second on December 21 at 00:00 UTC. This appears as a credit in Organization settings > Usage. Full launch offer terms below.

Does the launch offer also apply to the old experience?

No. The launch offer applies to usage in the new experience, including projects that were moved to it. Scans in the earlier version are charged as usual.

Claude Security plugin for Claude Code

What is the Claude Security plugin for Claude Code?

The Claude Security plugin for Claude Code is a separate feature, based on the same technology as Claude Security. It is available for users who wish to directly integrate the scanner into their workflows without relying on Anthropic’s hosted agent infrastructure, who have Zero Data Retention (ZDR) requirements, or who need model access through a third-party provider. Learn more here: Scan your codebase for vulnerabilities.

Does the Claude Security plugin for Claude Code use the same model?

Not necessarily. The plugin uses whichever models are available in your Claude Code account.

Scope of use: You will only use Claude Security to scan code that you or your company owns and to which you or your company holds all necessary rights to scan. You will not use Claude Security to scan code owned by or licensed from third parties, including but not limited to open source projects or repositories other than those included in your company’s codebase(s).

Claude Security launch offer terms

Who is eligible: Claude Enterprise organizations, including Claude Enterprise purchased through AWS Marketplace.

What you get: Up to $25,000 in promotional credits for Claude Security usage in each of two consecutive months. Each month runs from your organization’s start date to the same date the following month. Unused credits from a month don’t carry over.

How to get it: No sign-up is needed. Credits apply automatically to usage in the new Claude Security. Usage in projects from the earlier version isn’t covered until they’re migrated.

When it starts: Organizations that already have Claude Enterprise start on October 21, 2026. Organizations that sign up for Claude Enterprise after that date start on the day they sign up. The two months run whether or not your organization uses Claude Security.

When it ends: The offer ends at the end of the day on December 31, 2026 (UTC), even if your two months haven’t finished. Organizations that sign up after November 1, 2026 won’t get two full months.

How credits apply: Credits are used before your organization’s committed spend or usage credits, and are separate from any prepaid usage credits. After the credits are used or the offer ends, Claude Security usage is charged at direct token cost.

Where to see it: Organization admins can see the promotional balance in Organization Settings > Usage, under Services, or in Organization Settings > Claude Security, under Spend limit.

The Claude Promotional Credit Offer Terms also apply, including when credits can be forfeited and when the offer can change. If they differ from this article on this offer, this article controls.

What are customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK)?

Customer-managed encryption keys are available to eligible organizations on Enterprise plans and the Claude Platform.

A customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) lets your organization provision an encryption key in your own AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault and have Anthropic use it to encrypt certain data in Claude, such as your team’s chats, projects, and files. You keep full control of the key, and every operation Anthropic performs with your key is recorded in your cloud provider’s audit logs. CMEK is optional, and your organization can choose to enable it in place of the default encryption Anthropic provides.

For complete details, including what’s encrypted, what’s disabled or changed, limitations, and setup guides for each cloud provider, see Customer-managed encryption keys on Claude API Docs.

What happens to a user’s data when they are removed from a Team or Enterprise organization?

This article explains what happens to projects, chats, and skills when a member is removed from your Team or Enterprise plan organization.

Delete individual accounts within an organization

If you are a non-Owner member of a Team or Enterprise plan, you will need to contact an organization Owner to have your account removed.

Removing a user from your organization doesn’t delete their account or data. If you’re an Owner or Primary Owner, you can ask Support to permanently delete a removed user’s account and data:

  • If you need a copy of the user’s data, run an organization data export from the Primary Owner’s account first. The export still includes a removed user’s data.
  • If your organization provisions users through SCIM, remove the user in your identity provider (IdP). Otherwise, they may be provisioned again.
  • Contact Support from your own email address. Include the user’s email address, and confirm in writing that their account and data should be deleted.

Important: Deletion is permanent and can’t be undone.

Delete organization-level accounts

For help with deleting your organization’s Team or Enterprise plan, please reach out to our Support team. Note that organization level account deletion requests must be made by your account’s Primary Owner.

Will a user’s projects still be accessible after removing them?

Once a user is removed from your Team or Enterprise organization, whether remaining members can access their projects or not depends on the project’s visibility settings.

Private projects

If the project’s visibility was set to private, other members of the organization will not be able to access it once the team member has been removed from the account. If a team member knows they’re working on something in a private project they want to pass on, they will need to adjust the project’s permissions so either everyone in the organization can edit it, or invite specific users and grant them “Can edit” permissions.

Shared projects

If a deleted team member shared their project with the entire organization, it will appear under the “Team” tab where remaining members can view or edit the project, depending on their permissions. If the deleted team member shared the project with specific users only, it will appear under the “Shared with me” tab for those specific users after the member is removed from the organization.

Will a user’s chats still be accessible after removing them?

When a user is removed from your Team or Enterprise organization, remaining members will no longer be able to access their chats. This applies to chat snapshots that are shared with the organization. After the user who created the chat is removed, remaining members will see this message when they try to access any shared chat URLs: “Conversation not found. The requested conversation either doesn’t exist or you don’t have permission to access it.”

Note that the removed user’s data will still be included in any data exports run by your organization’s Primary Owner. For Enterprise organizations specifically, the removed user’s data will still be subject to any configured custom data retention settings. Custom data retention doesn’t cover memory of members who have left your organization.

Will a user’s skills still be accessible after removing them?

Removing a user from your Team or Enterprise organization doesn’t delete the skills they uploaded to their own account. Skills the user uploaded and never shared stay on their account and remain recoverable. If the user is later added back to the organization with the same email address, those skills will reappear under Customize > Skills, where they can download them.

What happens if a member is re-added to an organization?

If a team member is removed and later added back to the same organization using the same email address, previous chats, projects, and skills will be restored. The Primary Owner can also always export the member’s project data and chats (note that customer data retention settings may impact this).

To learn more about Anthropic’s data retention periods see here.

Who owns and manages the data of my team?

This article provides important information about your Claude for Work account associated with your organization’s Claude for Work plan (Team or Enterprise plans). It includes details about data access and control that were shared with you when your Claude for Work plan account was set up.

This article is about our commercial products such as Claude for Work and the Anthropic API. For our consumer products such as Claude Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, and when accounts from those plans use Claude Code, see here.

Account Management

Your organization’s designated Primary Owner manages your Work account and all associated data. This includes the ability to request access to your user data through data exports, which may contain your conversations with Claude, uploaded files, and usage patterns. Primary Owners can also remove your access to the Claude for Work plan account if necessary.

Your organization determines which Claude services and features you can access in your Claude for Work plan account and they may choose to limit certain functionality.

Governing Agreements

The use of your Claude for Work plan account is governed by the agreement between Anthropic and your organization. Please contact your Primary Owner for details of this agreement.

While Anthropic’s Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, and share personal information when acting as a data controller in providing the Claude services to your organization, please note that the Anthropic Consumer Terms of Service and Privacy Policy do not apply to the use of the Claude for Work plan where Anthropic acts as the data processor.

Organizational Policies

Your organization may have its own internal policies regarding usage of Claude for Work plan. Please refer to your Primary Owner for guidance.

Questions about Privacy

If you have any questions about data privacy in your Claude for Work plan account, we encourage you to contact your organization’s account owner(s).

Troubleshooting

Adapt to new model personas after deprecations

Model deprecations and retirements are routine parts of the model lifecycle. While we would like to keep past models publicly available as we continue to advance the frontier of safety and capabilities, maintenance overhead and capacity constraints do not currently allow this. We nonetheless recognize that losing access to models comes with costs to many users, particularly those who have come to value the unique character or capabilities of a specific model on a personal level. We aim to provide resources, tools, and guidance to such users to minimize these costs and make the transitions between models as smooth and seamless as possible.

Strategies and recommendations

Below are a set of strategies and recommendations for adapting to model transitions. Not all of them will be applicable in every circumstance, but in most cases we expect that some combination of these strategies can help to smooth the transition between models. We encourage you to experiment with these and other strategies to find what works best for you.

  • When a model deprecation is announced, we suggest experimenting with newer models as soon as possible. You can test different models and run side-by-side comparisons with the kinds of prompts and conversations that matter the most to you, to identify the best alternative model prior to retirement.
  • Enabling memory and allowing Claude to search past chats can help new models to learn and immediately adapt to your preferences and communication style.
  • Projects offer another means of personalization, and can include custom instructions for Claude as well as custom context, which again can help new models understand and adapt to your needs and preferences.
  • Using these personalization strategies can be thought of as giving feedback to new models. If you find that a new model is more or less talkative than you’d prefer, or has a different tone, you can shape the model’s behavior within a conversation, within a project, or across your entire account using the strategies above. If you’re not sure how to describe the qualities you’re looking for, you can ask Claude to review some of the conversations you’ve most appreciated and to craft instructions for itself based on those.
  • In addition to finding strategies for preserving features and styles of past models, we also encourage you to explore the changes that newer models bring. They often offer improved performance on complex topics, improved brainstorming and collaboration, better instruction following, and other improvements that you may find valuable, even if they come with a change.
  • Along with these practical strategies, we recommend maintaining a general awareness of the model lifecycle when relating to models; historically Anthropic has deprecated most models around a year after their initial release.

These strategies aren’t perfect and can only go so far toward preserving or replicating the unique experience of interacting with a particular model, which we recognize is intrinsically important to many users. We’re taking other early steps toward ensuring model preservation post-retirement, and someday aim to make past models publicly available again in some form.

Claude is producing links that don’t work and falsely claiming that it has sent emails or produced external documents. What’s going on?

In an attempt to be a helpful assistant, Claude can sometimes hallucinate its capabilities. Even if it claims otherwise, Claude does not have access to other tools or software that are not explicitly integrated, including email, word processors, or file transfers.

More information on hallucinations can be found here.

Claude is providing incorrect or misleading responses. What’s going on?

In an attempt to be a helpful assistant, Claude can occasionally produce responses that are incorrect or misleading.

This is known as “hallucinating” information, and it’s a byproduct of some of the current limitations of frontier Generative AI models, like Claude. For example, in some subject areas, Claude might not have been trained on the most-up-to-date information and may get confused when prompted about current events. Another example is that Claude can display quotes that may look authoritative or sound convincing, but are not grounded in fact. In other words, Claude can write things that might look correct but are very mistaken.

Users should not rely on Claude as a singular source of truth and should carefully scrutinize any high-stakes advice given by Claude.

When working with web search results, users should review Claude’s cited sources. Original websites may contain important context or details not included in Claude’s synthesis. Additionally, the quality of Claude’s responses depends on the underlying sources it references, so checking original content helps you identify any information that might be misinterpreted without the full context.

You can use the thumbs down button to let us know if a particular response was unhelpful, or write to us at [email protected] with your thoughts or suggestions.

To learn more about how Anthropic’s technology works and our research on developing safer, steerable, and more reliable models, we recommend visiting: anthropic.com

Troubleshoot Claude error messages

This article explains common error messages and warnings you may encounter when using Claude and provides guidance on how to address them.

Usage limit warnings and errors

Your plan has a weekly limit and, except on verified Ultra accounts, a five-hour session limit. Some plans have an additional weekly limit that applies specifically to Fable. Usage limit warnings appear when you’re approaching any of your plan’s limits: “Approaching session limit” or “Approaching weekly limit.” When the percentage is available, the warning shows how much of your limit you’ve used instead, for example “You’ve used X% of your weekly limit.”

If you reach a limit and don’t have usage credits enabled, you’ll see an error message letting you know when you can use Claude again: “5-hour limit reached - resets [time]” or “You’ve reached your weekly limit. It resets [day] at [time].”

Looking for ways to maximize your Claude usage? Refer to Usage limit best practices.

Usage credits

If you’re on a paid Claude plan with usage credits enabled in Usage settings, reaching any five-hour session limit or any of your weekly limits doesn’t stop your work. Your requests switch to pay-as-you-go pricing on usage credits and keep working until you reach your monthly spend limit or your usage credit balance runs out with auto-reload off. Instead of the error above, you’ll see “5-hour limit resets [time] - continuing with usage credits” or “Now using credits. Your plan limit resets [day] at [time]”.

Note: The warning that you’re approaching your limit may still be showing at the moment your usage switches to usage credits. It can look like you’ve been cut off, but your work continues, and the message changes to “Now using credits” once your next request goes through.

Refer to these articles for more information about this feature depending on your plan:

  • Manage usage credits for paid Claude plans
  • Manage usage credits for Team and seat-based Enterprise plans

Length limit errors

You may encounter a length limit error when your message to Claude exceeds the maximum input length allowed: “Your message will exceed the length limit for this chat. Try attaching fewer or smaller files or starting a new conversation.” This error indicates that your message is too long and needs to be shortened before sending it to Claude.

For users on paid plans with code execution enabled, Claude automatically manages long conversations by summarizing earlier messages when context limits are approached. This means most users will rarely encounter length limit errors during normal use. Your full chat history is preserved so Claude can reference it even after summarization. In rare cases where you still encounter this error (such as when sending a very large first message), you can:

  • Break your content into smaller chunks and process them separately
  • Summarize or extract key sections before sending to Claude
  • Use Claude to first identify the most relevant portions of your content
  • Start a new conversation

Login errors

If you see a generic error message when attempting to log in to your Claude account (e.g, “There was an error logging you in”), try the following troubleshooting steps:

  • Ensure you’re not using a VPN when accessing Claude.
  • Disable any browser extensions that you currently have active.
  • Clear your browser’s cache and cookies.

If you’re still seeing an error, check our status page for active incidents.

Capacity constraints

Capacity issues occur when Claude’s infrastructure experiences high demand system-wide. When capacity is constrained, you may see this message when chatting with Claude: “Due to unexpected capacity constraints, Claude is unable to respond to your message. Please try again soon.”

Important: Capacity constraints are not outages. The system is functioning normally but managing high demand across all users. These issues are temporary and typically resolve as demand patterns shift throughout the day. If you encounter this message, try again in a few minutes.

Capacity issues will not appear on our status page because they represent normal load management rather than technical problems.

Service incidents and outages

Service incidents are disruptions where Claude is unavailable or significantly degraded for all or most users. These represent actual technical problems with our systems. To check for confirmed incidents, visit status.claude.com, where you’ll find real-time updates on scope, impact, and resolution progress for any active incidents.

How to buy usage bundles
